questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone is dropped from a very high cliff. If the distance covered by the stone in the $n^{\text{th}}$ second of its descent is exactly equal to the total distance covered by it in the first $3$ seconds of its fall, what is the value of $n$?
questions.solution:
Distance covered in the $n^{\text{th}}$ second is given by $S_n = u + \dfrac{1}{2}g(2n - 1)$.

Since the stone is dropped, $u = 0$.

$S_n = \dfrac{1}{2}g(2n - 1)$

Total distance covered in the first $3$ seconds is given by $S = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}gt^2$.

$S = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}g(3)^2 = \dfrac{9}{2}g$

Given that $S_n = S$, we have:

$\dfrac{1}{2}g(2n - 1) = \dfrac{9}{2}g$

$2n - 1 = 9$

$2n = 10$

$n = 5$

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The position-time ($x-t$) graph for two cars, A and B, is shown in the given figure. Car A starts from a positive initial position and its graph makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the time axis. Car B starts from the origin and its graph makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the position axis. What is the ratio of the velocity of car A to the velocity of car B?
questions.solution:
The velocity of a particle is given by the slope of its position-time graph, i.e., $v = \tan \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle made by the graph with the time axis.

For car A, the angle with the time axis is $\theta_A = 30^{\circ}$.
Velocity of car A, $v_A = \tan 30^{\circ} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

For car B, the angle with the position axis is $30^{\circ}$. Therefore, the angle with the time axis is $\theta_B = 90^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 60^{\circ}$.
Velocity of car B, $v_B = \tan 60^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}$

The ratio of the velocity of car A to the velocity of car B is:
$\dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = \dfrac{1/\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Thus, the required ratio is $1 : 3$.

Answer: $1 : 3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An engine develops a constant power of $40\text{ kW}$. The total work done by the engine in $5\text{ minutes}$ is
questions.solution:
Given power $P = 40\text{ kW} = 40 \times 10^3\text{ W}$

Time $t = 5\text{ minutes} = 5 \times 60\text{ s} = 300\text{ s}$

Work done $W = P \times t$

$W = 40 \times 10^3 \times 300$

$W = 12 \times 10^6\text{ J} = 1.2 \times 10^7\text{ J}$

Answer: $1.2 \times 10^7\text{ J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A train of mass $2 \times 10^5 \text{ kg}$ is moving up an inclined track (where $\sin\theta = 0.01$) with a constant speed of $15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. The frictional resistance offered by the track is $5000 \text{ N}$. The power delivered by the train's engine is:
(Take $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$)
questions.solution:
Mass of the train, $m = 2 \times 10^5 \text{ kg}$

Speed of the train, $v = 15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

Frictional resistance, $f = 5000 \text{ N}$

Component of weight down the incline, $W_{\parallel} = mg \sin\theta$

$W_{\parallel} = (2 \times 10^5) \times 10 \times 0.01 = 20000 \text{ N}$

Since the train is moving with a constant speed, the net force is zero. The force exerted by the engine must balance the downward forces.

$F = W_{\parallel} + f$

$F = 20000 + 5000 = 25000 \text{ N}$

Power delivered by the engine is given by:

$P = F \times v$

$P = 25000 \times 15 = 375000 \text{ W} = 375 \text{ kW}$

Answer: $375 \text{ kW}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stationary satellite in deep space suddenly ruptures into three distinct modules due to an internal failure. The modules have masses $M$, $2M$, and $3M$. The module of mass $M$ is ejected along the positive x-axis with a speed of $120 \text{ m/s}$, while the module of mass $2M$ is ejected along the positive y-axis with a speed of $80 \text{ m/s}$. What is the speed of the heaviest module?
questions.solution:
Initial momentum of the satellite is zero.

By conservation of linear momentum:

$\vec{P}_1 + \vec{P}_2 + \vec{P}_3 = 0$

The momentum of the first module is $\vec{P}_1 = M(120 \hat{i}) = 120M \hat{i}$.

The momentum of the second module is $\vec{P}_2 = 2M(80 \hat{j}) = 160M \hat{j}$.

Let the velocity of the heaviest module of mass $3M$ be $\vec{v}$. Its momentum is $\vec{P}_3 = 3M \vec{v}$.

Substituting the values:

$120M \hat{i} + 160M \hat{j} + 3M \vec{v} = 0$

$3M \vec{v} = -120M \hat{i} - 160M \hat{j}$

$\vec{v} = -40 \hat{i} - \dfrac{160}{3} \hat{j}$

The speed of the heaviest module is the magnitude of its velocity:

$|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{(-40)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{160}{3}\right)^2}$

$|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{1600 + \dfrac{25600}{9}}$

$|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{\dfrac{14400 + 25600}{9}}$

$|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{\dfrac{40000}{9}} = \dfrac{200}{3} \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $\dfrac{200}{3} \text{ m/s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two uniform solid spheres of the same material having radii $R$ and $2R$ are placed such that they are in contact with each other. What is the distance of the center of mass of this two-sphere system from the center of the smaller sphere?
questions.solution:
Let the density of the material be $\rho$.

Mass of the smaller sphere, $M_1 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho = M$

Mass of the larger sphere, $M_2 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (2R)^3 \rho = 8M$

The distance between the centers of the two spheres is $d = R + 2R = 3R$.

Taking the center of the smaller sphere as the origin $(0,0)$, the coordinates of the centers are $x_1 = 0$ and $x_2 = 3R$.

The position of the center of mass is given by:

$x_{cm} = \dfrac{M_1 x_1 + M_2 x_2}{M_1 + M_2}$

$x_{cm} = \dfrac{M(0) + 8M(3R)}{M + 8M}$

$x_{cm} = \dfrac{24MR}{9M} = \dfrac{8R}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{8R}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A space probe measures the gravitational force on a $40\text{ g}$ sample of rock to be $0.064\text{ N}$ at the surface of a newly discovered moon. What is the gravitational field strength at the surface of this moon?
questions.solution:
Given mass of the rock sample, $m = 40\text{ g} = 0.04\text{ kg}$

Gravitational force on the sample, $F = 0.064\text{ N}$

The gravitational field strength $g$ is given by the force per unit mass:

$g = \dfrac{F}{m}$

$g = \dfrac{0.064}{0.04}$

$g = 1.6\text{ N kg}^{-1}$

Answer: $1.6\text{ N kg}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two soap bubbles of unequal radii are connected by a narrow hollow tube. Which of the following correctly describes the flow of air between them?
options: Air flows from the smaller bubble to the larger bubble.
Air flows from the larger bubble to the smaller bubble.
Air does not flow as the system is already in pressure equilibrium.
Air flows from the larger to the smaller bubble until their sizes become equal.
questions.solution:
The excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius $R$ is given by $\Delta P = \dfrac{4T}{R}$, where $T$ is the surface tension.

Let the radius of the smaller bubble be $r$ and the larger bubble be $R$, with $r \lt R$.

The pressure inside the smaller bubble is $P_1 = P_0 + \dfrac{4T}{r}$ and inside the larger bubble is $P_2 = P_0 + \dfrac{4T}{R}$.

Since $r \lt R$, we have $\dfrac{4T}{r} \gt \dfrac{4T}{R}$, which implies $P_1 \gt P_2$.

Air always flows from a region of higher pressure to a region of lower pressure. Therefore, air will flow from the smaller bubble to the larger bubble.

Answer: Air flows from the smaller bubble to the larger bubble.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An air bubble is released from rest at the bottom of a tall glass column filled with a highly viscous liquid. As the bubble rises, it experiences a constant buoyant force, its own weight, and a viscous drag force that obeys Stokes' law.

Which of the graphs shown below best represents the variation of the bubble's upward acceleration ($a$) as a function of its upward velocity ($v$) until it reaches terminal velocity?
questions.solution:
Let the mass of the air bubble be $m$ and its radius be $r$.

The forces acting on the bubble as it rises are:
1. Upward buoyant force, $F_B$ (given as constant)
2. Downward weight, $W = mg$
3. Downward viscous drag force, $F_v$

According to Stokes' law, the viscous drag force is proportional to the velocity $v$ of the bubble:
$F_v = 6\pi\eta r v = kv$
where $k = 6\pi\eta r$ is a positive constant.

The net upward force $F_{\text{net}}$ on the bubble is:
$F_{\text{net}} = F_B - W - F_v$
$ma = F_B - mg - kv$

Dividing by $m$, we get the upward acceleration $a$ as a function of upward velocity $v$:
$a = \dfrac{F_B - mg}{m} - \left(\dfrac{k}{m}\right)v$

Let $a_0 = \dfrac{F_B - mg}{m}$ and $c = \dfrac{k}{m}$. Since $F_B$, $m$, $g$, and $k$ are constants, $a_0$ and $c$ are also positive constants. The equation simplifies to:
$a = a_0 - cv$

This is the equation of a straight line with a positive y-intercept ($a_0$) and a negative slope ($-c$).

Looking at the given graphs:
- Graph (P) represents a straight line with a negative slope and a positive intercept, which perfectly matches our derived equation.
- The acceleration becomes zero when the bubble reaches its terminal velocity $v_1 = \dfrac{a_0}{c}$.

Therefore, Graph (P) best represents the variation of the bubble's upward acceleration as a function of its upward velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An ideal gas is compressed from a common initial state $I$ to a final volume $V_f$ via three different processes as shown in the $P-V$ diagram. The processes are known to be isothermal, adiabatic, and isobaric. Which curve correctly represents the adiabatic compression?
options: Either Curve 1 or 2 depending on the atomicity of the gas
questions.solution:
For an ideal gas, the equations for the given processes are:
Isobaric: $P = \text{constant}$
Isothermal: $PV = \text{constant}$
Adiabatic: $PV^\gamma = \text{constant}$

Curve 3 is a horizontal line ($P = \text{constant}$), so it represents the isobaric process.

The slope of the $P-V$ curve is given by $\dfrac{dP}{dV}$.
For an isothermal process: $\dfrac{dP}{dV} = -\dfrac{P}{V}$
For an adiabatic process: $\dfrac{dP}{dV} = -\gamma \dfrac{P}{V}$

Since the heat capacity ratio $\gamma \gt 1$, the magnitude of the slope for the adiabatic curve is greater than that for the isothermal curve. This means the adiabatic curve is steeper.

During compression, the volume decreases. Starting from a common initial state $I$, the steeper curve will rise to a higher final pressure for the same final volume $V_f$.

From the given graph, at $V = V_f$, the pressure for Curve 1 is greater than the pressure for Curve 2. Therefore, Curve 1 represents the adiabatic compression and Curve 2 represents the isothermal compression.

Answer: Curve 1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two uniform strings A and B made of the same material have lengths in the ratio $1:3$ and diameters in the ratio $2:1$. If they are subjected to identical tension, what is the ratio of the speeds of transverse waves in string A to that in string B?
questions.solution:
The speed of a transverse wave in a string is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$, where $T$ is the tension and $\mu$ is the linear mass density.

The linear mass density can be expressed as $\mu = \rho A = \rho \dfrac{\pi D^2}{4}$, where $\rho$ is the density of the material and $D$ is the diameter of the string.

Since both strings are made of the same material and subjected to identical tension, $T$ and $\rho$ are the same for both strings.

Thus, the speed of the transverse wave is inversely proportional to the diameter of the string, $v \propto \dfrac{1}{D}$.

The ratio of the speeds of transverse waves in string A to that in string B is:

$\dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = \dfrac{D_B}{D_A}$

Given that the ratio of diameters is $D_A : D_B = 2 : 1$, we get:

$\dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

The lengths of the strings do not affect the speed of the transverse waves.

Answer: $1:2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is the magnitude of the component of the electric field parallel to an equipotential surface?
options: Equal to the net electric field
Equal to the perpendicular component of the field
Dependent on the local surface charge density
questions.solution:
By definition, the electric potential $V$ is constant everywhere on an equipotential surface.

The component of the electric field along any direction is given by $E = -\dfrac{dV}{dr}$.

For any displacement $dr$ parallel to the equipotential surface, the change in potential $dV = 0$.

Therefore, the component of the electric field parallel to the equipotential surface is $E_{\parallel} = -\dfrac{0}{dr} = 0$.

This implies that the electric field is always perpendicular to the equipotential surface, and its parallel component is zero.

Answer: Zero

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two isolated solid metallic spheres $A$ and $B$ have radii in the ratio $1 : 2$. They are given net charges in the ratio $3 : 4$. What will be the ratio of the electric potentials at their surfaces, $V_A : V_B$?
questions.solution:
The electric potential at the surface of an isolated solid metallic sphere is given by $V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{R}$.

For spheres $A$ and $B$, the ratio of their potentials is:

$\dfrac{V_A}{V_B} = \dfrac{Q_A}{Q_B} \times \dfrac{R_B}{R_A}$

Given $\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\dfrac{Q_A}{Q_B} = \dfrac{3}{4}$, substituting these values:

$\dfrac{V_A}{V_B} = \dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{2}{1} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

The ratio of the electric potentials is $3 : 2$.

Answer: $3 : 2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A piece of copper and a piece of germanium are cooled from room temperature ($300\text{ K}$) to $80\text{ K}$. Which of the following statements is correct regarding their electrical resistances?
options: The resistance of both copper and germanium will decrease.
The resistance of copper will decrease while that of germanium will increase.
The resistance of copper will increase while that of germanium will decrease.
The resistance of both copper and germanium will increase.
questions.solution:
Copper is a metallic conductor. For metals, the temperature coefficient of resistivity is positive. As temperature decreases, the thermal agitation of atoms decreases, which increases the relaxation time of free electrons. This leads to a decrease in electrical resistance.

Germanium is a semiconductor. For semiconductors, the number density of charge carriers (electrons and holes) decreases exponentially with a decrease in temperature ($n \propto e^{-E_g / 2kT}$). This reduction in charge carriers leads to an increase in electrical resistance.

Thus, when cooled from $300\text{ K}$ to $80\text{ K}$, the resistance of copper decreases while that of germanium increases.

Answer: The resistance of copper will decrease while that of germanium will increase.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform nichrome wire of length $4.0\ \text{m}$ and cross-sectional area $0.2\ \text{mm}^2$ has an electrical resistance of $5.0\ \Omega$. If an electric field of $1.5\ \text{V m}^{-1}$ is established along its length, the current density in the wire is:
questions.solution:
Given $l = 4.0\ \text{m}$, $A = 0.2\ \text{mm}^2 = 2 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{m}^2$, $R = 5.0\ \Omega$, and $E = 1.5\ \text{V m}^{-1}$.

The potential difference across the wire is:

$V = E \times l = 1.5 \times 4.0 = 6.0\ \text{V}$

The current flowing through the wire is:

$I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{6.0}{5.0} = 1.2\ \text{A}$

The current density $J$ is given by:

$J = \dfrac{I}{A} = \dfrac{1.2}{2 \times 10^{-7}} = 6 \times 10^6\ \text{A m}^{-2}$

Answer: $6 \times 10^6\ \text{A m}^{-2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long tightly wound solenoid is used in a laboratory to generate a uniform magnetic field of $25.12\text{ mT}$ at its center. If the solenoid has $500\text{ turns}$ per $10\text{ cm}$ of its length, what is the magnitude of the steady current flowing through it? (Take $\pi = 3.14$)
questions.solution:
The magnetic field at the center of a long tightly wound solenoid is given by the formula:

$B = \mu_0 n I$

where $n$ is the number of turns per unit length and $I$ is the current.

Given:
$B = 25.12 \text{ mT} = 25.12 \times 10^{-3} \text{ T}$
$n = \dfrac{500}{10 \text{ cm}} = \dfrac{500}{10 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}} = 5000 \text{ turns/m}$
$\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}$

Substituting the values into the formula:

$25.12 \times 10^{-3} = (4 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-7}) \times 5000 \times I$

$25.12 \times 10^{-3} = 12.56 \times 10^{-7} \times 5000 \times I$

$25.12 \times 10^{-3} = 6.28 \times 10^{-3} \times I$

$I = \dfrac{25.12 \times 10^{-3}}{6.28 \times 10^{-3}}$

$I = 4 \text{ A}$

Answer: $4\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular loop of sides $50\text{ cm}$ and $40\text{ cm}$ has a resistance of $5\ \Omega$. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field of $1.5\text{ T}$. If the plane of the loop makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the direction of the magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is:
questions.solution:
The area of the rectangular loop is given by:

$A = 50\text{ cm} \times 40\text{ cm} = 2000\text{ cm}^2 = 0.2\text{ m}^2$

The plane of the loop makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the magnetic field. The angle $\theta$ between the area vector (normal to the plane) and the magnetic field is:

$\theta = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$

The magnetic flux $\Phi$ through the loop is:

$\Phi = BA \cos\theta$

Substituting the given values:

$\Phi = 1.5 \times 0.2 \times \cos 60^\circ$

$\Phi = 0.3 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.15\text{ Wb}$

Answer: $0.15\text{ Wb}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The alternating current flowing through a circuit is given by the equation $i = 10 \sin(50\pi t)\text{ A}$. The root mean square (rms) value of this current is:
questions.solution:
The given equation for the alternating current is $i = 10 \sin(50\pi t)$ A.

Comparing this with the standard equation of alternating current $i = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$, the peak value of the current is $I_0 = 10$ A.

The root mean square (rms) value of the current is given by the relation:

$I_{rms} = \dfrac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}$

Substituting the value of $I_0$:

$I_{rms} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{2}} = 5\sqrt{2}$ A.

Answer: $5\sqrt{2}\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave travels through a medium having relative permittivity $\epsilon_r$ and relative permeability $\mu_r$. If a new medium is chosen such that its relative permittivity is $2\epsilon_r$ and relative permeability is $\dfrac{\mu_r}{2}$, the speed of the electromagnetic wave in the new medium compared to the original medium will:
questions.solution:
The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium is given by $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \epsilon}} = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$.

For the original medium, $v_1 = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$.

For the new medium, the relative permittivity is $2\epsilon_r$ and the relative permeability is $\dfrac{\mu_r}{2}$.

The speed in the new medium is $v_2 = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{\mu_r}{2}\right) (2\epsilon_r)}} = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$.

Thus, $v_2 = v_1$.

The speed of the electromagnetic wave remains the same.

Answer: remain the same

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A narrow beam of light travelling in air strikes the flat surface of a transparent liquid at an angle of incidence of $45^{\circ}$. If the refractive index of the liquid is $\sqrt{2}$, what is the angle of deviation suffered by the light ray upon refraction?
questions.solution:
Using Snell's law at the air-liquid interface:

$n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r$

Substituting the given values:

$1 \times \sin 45^{\circ} = \sqrt{2} \times \sin r$

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} \sin r$

$\sin r = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$r = 30^{\circ}$

The angle of deviation $\delta$ is given by:

$\delta = i - r$

$\delta = 45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 15^{\circ}$

Answer: $15^{\circ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A Young's double slit apparatus is illuminated simultaneously by a light source containing two wavelengths, $\lambda_1 = 420 \text{ nm}$ and $\lambda_2 = 560 \text{ nm}$. The distance between the two slits is $1.0 \text{ mm}$ and the screen is placed at a distance of $1.5 \text{ m}$ from the slits. What is the minimum non-zero distance from the central maximum where the bright fringes of both wavelengths coincide?
questions.solution:
Let the $n_1$-th bright fringe of $\lambda_1$ coincide with the $n_2$-th bright fringe of $\lambda_2$. The position of the $n$-th bright fringe from the central maximum is given by $y = \dfrac{n \lambda D}{d}$.

For the fringes to coincide, $y_1 = y_2$:

$\dfrac{n_1 \lambda_1 D}{d} = \dfrac{n_2 \lambda_2 D}{d}$

$n_1 \lambda_1 = n_2 \lambda_2$

Substituting the given wavelengths:

$n_1 (420) = n_2 (560)$

$\dfrac{n_1}{n_2} = \dfrac{560}{420} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

For the minimum non-zero distance, $n_1$ and $n_2$ must be the smallest possible integers. Thus, $n_1 = 4$ and $n_2 = 3$.

The minimum distance $y$ is:

$y = \dfrac{n_1 \lambda_1 D}{d}$

$y = \dfrac{4 \times 420 \times 10^{-9} \times 1.5}{1.0 \times 10^{-3}}$

$y = 2520 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$

$y = 2.52 \text{ mm}$

Answer: $2.52 \text{ mm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If $E_H$ represents the total energy of an electron in the second Bohr orbit of a hydrogen atom and $E_{He}$ represents the total energy of an electron in the third Bohr orbit of a singly ionized helium atom ($He^+$), then the ratio $E_H : E_{He}$ is:
questions.solution:
The total energy of an electron in the $n$-th Bohr orbit of a hydrogen-like atom is given by $E = -13.6 \dfrac{Z^2}{n^2} \text{ eV}$.

For the hydrogen atom ($Z = 1$) in the second Bohr orbit ($n = 2$):
$E_H = -13.6 \times \dfrac{1^2}{2^2} = -\dfrac{13.6}{4} \text{ eV}$

For the singly ionized helium atom ($He^+$, $Z = 2$) in the third Bohr orbit ($n = 3$):
$E_{He} = -13.6 \times \dfrac{2^2}{3^2} = -13.6 \times \dfrac{4}{9} \text{ eV}$

Taking the ratio of the two energies:
$\dfrac{E_H}{E_{He}} = \dfrac{-\dfrac{13.6}{4}}{-13.6 \times \dfrac{4}{9}} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{9}{4} = \dfrac{9}{16}$

The ratio $E_H : E_{He}$ is $9 : 16$.

Answer: $9 : 16$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Identify the missing particle $X$ in the following nuclear reaction:

$^{27}_{13}\text{Al} + ^{4}_{2}\text{He} \rightarrow ^{30}_{15}\text{P} + X$
questions.solution:
Let the missing particle $X$ have mass number $A$ and atomic number $Z$.

The nuclear reaction is:
$^{27}_{13}\text{Al} + ^{4}_{2}\text{He} \rightarrow ^{30}_{15}\text{P} + ^{A}_{Z}X$

Applying the law of conservation of mass number:
$27 + 4 = 30 + A$
$31 = 30 + A$
$A = 1$

Applying the law of conservation of atomic number:
$13 + 2 = 15 + Z$
$15 = 15 + Z$
$Z = 0$

The particle with mass number $A = 1$ and atomic number $Z = 0$ is a neutron ($^{1}_{0}\text{n}$).

Answer: Neutron

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the given circuit, $D_1$ and $D_2$ are ideal $p-n$ junction diodes. What will be the reading of the ideal voltmeter $V$ connected across $D_2$?
questions.solution:
In the given circuit, the positive terminal of the $12\text{ V}$ battery is connected to the left side.

Diode $D_1$ is forward-biased as its p-side faces the higher potential. Diode $D_2$ is reverse-biased as its n-side faces the higher potential.

Since $D_2$ is an ideal diode in reverse bias, it acts as an open circuit. The ideal voltmeter also has infinite resistance, so no current flows through the circuit ($I = 0$).

The voltage drop across the resistor $R$ is $V_R = I R = 0\text{ V}$.

The voltage drop across the ideal forward-biased diode $D_1$ is $0\text{ V}$.

Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law:

$12 - V_R - V_{D1} - V_{D2} = 0$

$12 - 0 - 0 - V_{D2} = 0$

$V_{D2} = 12\text{ V}$

The voltmeter reads the potential difference across $D_2$, which is $12\text{ V}$.

Answer: $12\text{ V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An alternating voltage of $200 \text{ V}$ is applied across a series combination of a resistor, an inductor, and a capacitor. If the voltage drop across the resistor is $100 \text{ V}$ and the voltage across the capacitor is $50 \text{ V}$, determine the voltage across the inductor.
questions.solution:
In a series RLC circuit, the applied alternating voltage $V$ is given by the phasor sum of the voltages across the resistor, inductor, and capacitor:

$V^2 = V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2$

Substituting the given values $V = 200 \text{ V}$, $V_R = 100 \text{ V}$, and $V_C = 50 \text{ V}$:

$(200)^2 = (100)^2 + (V_L - 50)^2$

$40000 = 10000 + (V_L - 50)^2$

$(V_L - 50)^2 = 30000$

$V_L - 50 = \pm 100\sqrt{3}$

$V_L = 50 \pm 100\sqrt{3}$

Since the RMS voltage across the inductor must be positive, we take the positive root:

$V_L = 50 + 100\sqrt{3} = 50(2\sqrt{3} + 1) \text{ V}$

Answer: $50(2\sqrt{3} + 1) \text{ V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a certain photosensitive surface is illuminated with monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, the maximum velocity of the emitted photoelectrons is $v$. When the same surface is illuminated by light of wavelength $\dfrac{3\lambda}{4}$, the maximum velocity of the photoelectrons is observed to be $2v$. The threshold wavelength for this surface is:
questions.solution:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy is $K_{max} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$, where $\lambda_0$ is the threshold wavelength.

For the first case, when the wavelength is $\lambda$ and maximum velocity is $v$:

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$

For the second case, when the wavelength is $\dfrac{3\lambda}{4}$ and maximum velocity is $2v$:

$\dfrac{1}{2}m(2v)^2 = \dfrac{hc}{\left(\dfrac{3\lambda}{4}\right)} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$

$4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2\right) = \dfrac{4hc}{3\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$

Substituting the value of $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$ from the first equation into the second equation:

$4\left(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}\right) = \dfrac{4hc}{3\lambda} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$

Dividing the entire equation by $hc$:

$\dfrac{4}{\lambda} - \dfrac{4}{\lambda_0} = \dfrac{4}{3\lambda} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_0}$

Rearranging the terms:

$\dfrac{4}{\lambda} - \dfrac{4}{3\lambda} = \dfrac{4}{\lambda_0} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_0}$

$\dfrac{12 - 4}{3\lambda} = \dfrac{3}{\lambda_0}$

$\dfrac{8}{3\lambda} = \dfrac{3}{\lambda_0}$

$\lambda_0 = \dfrac{9\lambda}{8}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car travels at a constant speed of $34.5\text{ m/s}$ for a duration of $15\text{ s}$. The total distance covered by the car, expressed with the correct number of significant figures, is:
questions.solution:
The distance covered is given by the product of speed and time.

$d = v \times t$

$d = 34.5 \times 15 = 517.5\text{ m}$

The number of significant figures in the speed ($34.5\text{ m/s}$) is $3$.

The number of significant figures in the time ($15\text{ s}$) is $2$.

According to the rules of significant figures for multiplication, the final result must be reported to the same number of significant figures as the measurement with the least number of significant figures. Therefore, the result must be rounded to $2$ significant figures.

Rounding $517.5$ to $2$ significant figures gives $520\text{ m}$, which is expressed in scientific notation as $5.2 \times 10^{2}\text{ m}$.

Answer: $5.2 \times 10^{2}\text{ m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched from the surface of the earth with an initial speed $u$. At the highest point of its trajectory, its speed is found to be $\dfrac{u}{2}$. What is the angle of projection of the projectile with respect to the vertical?
questions.solution:
Let the angle of projection with respect to the vertical be $\phi$.

The horizontal component of the initial velocity is $u \sin \phi$.

During projectile motion, the horizontal component of velocity remains constant. At the highest point of the trajectory, the vertical component of velocity is zero, so the speed of the projectile is purely horizontal.

Speed at the highest point $= u \sin \phi$

Given that the speed at the highest point is $\dfrac{u}{2}$, we have:

$u \sin \phi = \dfrac{u}{2}$

$\sin \phi = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\phi = 30^\circ$

Answer: $30^\circ$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Suppose the intermolecular forces in $1.7\text{ kg}$ of liquid ammonia ($NH_3$) completely vanish, causing it to behave as an ideal gas. The volume occupied by this gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP) will be:
questions.solution:
Mass of $NH_3 = 1.7\text{ kg} = 1700\text{ g}$

Molar mass of $NH_3 = 14 + 3 = 17\text{ g/mol}$

Number of moles $n = \dfrac{1700}{17} = 100\text{ mol}$

Volume of $1\text{ mole}$ of an ideal gas at STP is $22.4\text{ L} = 22.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3$

Total volume $V = n \times 22.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3$

$V = 100 \times 22.4 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3 = 2.24\text{ m}^3$

Answer: $2.24\text{ m}^3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two simple pendulums are suspended from the same rigid support and start oscillating in phase from their mean positions. They are observed to be in phase again at the mean position for the first time after the shorter pendulum has completed exactly $7$ oscillations. What is the ratio of the length of the longer pendulum to that of the shorter pendulum?
questions.solution:
Let $T_S$ and $T_L$ be the time periods of the shorter and longer pendulums respectively, and $L_S$ and $L_L$ be their lengths.

For the two pendulums to be in phase again at the mean position for the first time, they must have completed an integer number of oscillations, and the shorter pendulum must have completed exactly one more oscillation than the longer pendulum.

Given that the shorter pendulum completes $7$ oscillations, the longer pendulum must have completed $7 - 1 = 6$ oscillations in the same time interval.

Equating the total time taken:

$7 T_S = 6 T_L$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{T_L}{T_S} = \dfrac{7}{6}$

The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$, which implies $L \propto T^2$.

Therefore, the ratio of their lengths is:

$\dfrac{L_L}{L_S} = \left(\dfrac{T_L}{T_S}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{7}{6}\right)^2 = \dfrac{49}{36}$

Answer: $49 : 36$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An ideal electric dipole of dipole moment $\vec{p}$ is placed at the origin, aligned along the positive x-axis. Two points, A and B, are located on the positive y-axis at distances $d$ and $3d$ from the origin, respectively, as shown in the figure.

If the magnitude of the electric field at point A is $E_0$, what is the magnitude of the electric field at point B?
questions.solution:
The electric field due to an ideal (short) dipole at a point on its equatorial axis is given by:

$E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{p}{r^3}$

Thus, the magnitude of the electric field is inversely proportional to the cube of the distance from the dipole, $E \propto \dfrac{1}{r^3}$.

For point A at distance $r = d$:

$E_A = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{p}{d^3} = E_0$

For point B at distance $r = 3d$:

$E_B = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{p}{(3d)^3}$

$E_B = \dfrac{1}{27} \left( \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{p}{d^3} \right)$

$E_B = \dfrac{E_0}{27}$

Answer: $\dfrac{E_0}{27}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the given circuit, the two-way switch $S$ is initially kept at position 1 for a long time, fully charging the capacitor $C_1 = 4\ \mu\text{F}$ using a $50\ \text{V}$ battery. The switch is then shifted to position 2, disconnecting the battery and connecting $C_1$ to an initially uncharged capacitor $C_2 = 6\ \mu\text{F}$. The amount of electrostatic energy dissipated as heat during the redistribution of charge is:
questions.solution:
When the switch is at position 1, capacitor $C_1$ is charged to potential $V_1 = 50\ \text{V}$.

When the switch is shifted to position 2, $C_1$ is connected across the initially uncharged capacitor $C_2$ ($V_2 = 0$).

The electrostatic energy dissipated as heat during the redistribution of charge is given by the formula:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} (V_1 - V_2)^2$

Substituting the given values $C_1 = 4\ \mu\text{F}$, $C_2 = 6\ \mu\text{F}$, $V_1 = 50\ \text{V}$, and $V_2 = 0\ \text{V}$:

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{(4 \times 10^{-6}) \times (6 \times 10^{-6})}{(4 + 6) \times 10^{-6}} \times (50 - 0)^2$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{24 \times 10^{-12}}{10 \times 10^{-6}} \times 2500$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2.4 \times 10^{-6} \times 2500$

$\Delta U = 1.2 \times 10^{-6} \times 2500$

$\Delta U = 3000 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{J}$

$\Delta U = 3 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{J}$

Answer: $3 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student sets up the Wheatstone bridge circuit shown in the figure to measure an unknown resistance $R_x$, which is known to be approximately $50\ \Omega$. The bridge is balanced by adjusting the variable standard resistance $R_s$. To ensure the maximum sensitivity of the bridge (and hence the most precise measurement of $R_x$), which of the following pairs of values should be chosen for the ratio arms $R_1$ and $R_2$?
questions.solution:
For a Wheatstone bridge, the sensitivity is defined as the deflection of the galvanometer per unit fractional change in the unknown resistance. The bridge is most sensitive when the resistances of all four of its arms are of the same order of magnitude (i.e., approximately equal).

Given that the unknown resistance $R_x$ is approximately $50\ \Omega$, the standard resistance $R_s$ will also be adjusted to approximately $50\ \Omega$ to achieve balance if the ratio arms are equal.

To ensure maximum sensitivity, the ratio arms $R_1$ and $R_2$ should also be chosen to be approximately equal to $R_x$.

Therefore, choosing $R_1 = 50\ \Omega$ and $R_2 = 50\ \Omega$ makes all four arms of the bridge approximately equal ($R_1 \approx R_2 \approx R_x \approx R_s \approx 50\ \Omega$), which provides the most precise measurement.

Answer: $R_1 = 50\ \Omega$, $R_2 = 50\ \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular coil of $2500$ turns and dimensions $80\text{ cm} \times 50\text{ cm}$ is rotated at a constant angular speed of $200\text{ rad s}^{-1}$ about its vertical axis of symmetry. At this location, the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field is $3 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$ and the vertical component is $4 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$. If the electrical resistance of the coil is $2\Omega$, what will be the maximum induced current in the coil?
questions.solution:
Since the coil is rotated about its vertical axis of symmetry, its area vector always lies in the horizontal plane. Therefore, the vertical component of the earth's magnetic field ($B_V$) is always parallel to the plane of the coil and does not contribute to the magnetic flux. Only the horizontal component ($B_H$) contributes to the changing magnetic flux.

The maximum induced EMF in the coil is given by:
$E_{\text{max}} = N A B_H \omega$

Given values:
$N = 2500$
$A = 80\text{ cm} \times 50\text{ cm} = 0.8\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m} = 0.4\text{ m}^2$
$B_H = 3 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$
$\omega = 200\text{ rad s}^{-1}$

Substituting the values into the formula:
$E_{\text{max}} = 2500 \times 0.4 \times 3 \times 10^{-5} \times 200$
$E_{\text{max}} = 1000 \times 6000 \times 10^{-5} = 6\text{ V}$

The maximum induced current in the coil is:
$I_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{E_{\text{max}}}{R}$

Given the resistance $R = 2\Omega$:
$I_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3\text{ A}$

Answer: $3\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An alternating voltage given by $V = 120 \sin(2000t)$ is applied across a series LCR circuit containing an inductor of $0.1\text{ H}$, a capacitor of $10\ \mu\text{F}$, and a resistor of $40\ \Omega$. Let $\nu_0$ be the resonant frequency of this circuit. Which of the following options correctly gives the value of $\nu_0$ and describes the phase of the current relative to the applied voltage at the given source frequency?
questions.solution:
Given $V = 120 \sin(2000t)$, the angular frequency of the source is $\omega = 2000 ext{ rad/s}$.

The resonant angular frequency is given by $\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.

Substituting the given values $L = 0.1 ext{ H}$ and $C = 10\ \mu ext{F} = 10^{-5} ext{ F}$:

$\omega_0 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{0.1 imes 10^{-5}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-6}}} = 1000 ext{ rad/s}$

The resonant frequency $ u_0$ is:

$ u_0 = \dfrac{\omega_0}{2\pi} = \dfrac{1000}{2\pi} = \dfrac{500}{\pi} ext{ Hz}$

To find the phase relationship at the source frequency $\omega = 2000 ext{ rad/s}$, we calculate the inductive and capacitive reactances:

$X_L = \omega L = 2000 imes 0.1 = 200\ \Omega$

$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{2000 imes 10^{-5}} = 50\ \Omega$

Since $X_L \gt X_C$, the circuit is predominantly inductive at this frequency.

In an inductive circuit, the current lags the applied voltage.

Answer: $ u_0 = \dfrac{500}{\pi} ext{ Hz}$; current lags the voltage

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A monochromatic ray of light has a wavelength of $480 \text{ nm}$ in a transparent medium $X$ and $600 \text{ nm}$ in a transparent medium $Y$. When the light ray travels from medium $X$ to medium $Y$, the critical angle for total internal reflection at their interface is:
questions.solution:
The refractive index of a medium is inversely proportional to the wavelength of light in it, $n \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda}$.

The refractive indices of medium $X$ and medium $Y$ are $n_X = \dfrac{c}{f \lambda_X}$ and $n_Y = \dfrac{c}{f \lambda_Y}$.

The critical angle $\theta_c$ for total internal reflection at the interface when light travels from a denser medium $X$ to a rarer medium $Y$ is given by $\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{n_Y}{n_X}$.

Substituting the expressions for refractive indices, we get $\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{\lambda_X}{\lambda_Y}$.

Given $\lambda_X = 480 \text{ nm}$ and $\lambda_Y = 600 \text{ nm}$, we have $\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{480}{600} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Therefore, $\theta_c = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)$.

Answer: $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two different stable nuclei have their nuclear radii in the ratio $3 : 2$. If the heavier nucleus has a mass number of $162$, what is the mass number of the lighter nucleus?
questions.solution:
The nuclear radius $R$ is related to the mass number $A$ by the formula $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$.

Let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be the radii of the heavier and lighter nuclei respectively, and $A_1$ and $A_2$ be their mass numbers.

Given $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and $A_1 = 162$.

Using the relation, we have $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \left(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2}\right)^{1/3}$

$\dfrac{3}{2} = \left(\dfrac{162}{A_2}\right)^{1/3}$

Cubing both sides, we get:

$\dfrac{27}{8} = \dfrac{162}{A_2}$

$A_2 = \dfrac{162 \times 8}{27}$

$A_2 = 6 \times 8 = 48$

The mass number of the lighter nucleus is $48$.

Answer: $48$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What mass of an $85\%$ pure sample of $Mg(OH)_2$ is required to completely neutralize $250\text{ mL}$ of a $0.4\text{ M } HNO_3$ solution according to the given reaction?

$Mg(OH)_{2(s)} + 2HNO_{3(aq)} \rightarrow Mg(NO_3)_{2(aq)} + 2H_2O_{(l)}$

[Calculate up to the second place of decimal point. Atomic masses: $Mg = 24$, $O = 16$, $H = 1$]
questions.solution:
Moles of $HNO_3 = M \times V = 0.4 \times \dfrac{250}{1000} = 0.1\text{ mol}$

From the balanced chemical equation, $1\text{ mol}$ of $Mg(OH)_2$ neutralizes $2\text{ mol}$ of $HNO_3$.

Moles of $Mg(OH)_2$ required = $\dfrac{0.1}{2} = 0.05\text{ mol}$

Molar mass of $Mg(OH)_2 = 24 + 2 \times (16 + 1) = 58\text{ g/mol}$

Mass of pure $Mg(OH)_2$ required = $0.05 \times 58 = 2.9\text{ g}$

Since the sample is $85\%$ pure, the mass of the sample required is given by:

$m \times \dfrac{85}{100} = 2.9$

$m = \dfrac{2.9 \times 100}{85} = 3.41\text{ g}$

Answer: $3.41\text{ g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: According to IUPAC nomenclature, what is the three-letter temporary symbol for the element with atomic number $120$?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of the element is $120$.

According to IUPAC systematic nomenclature, the roots for the digits are:
$1 \rightarrow$ un
$2 \rightarrow$ bi
$0 \rightarrow$ nil

Combining these roots, the temporary IUPAC name for the element is unbinilium.

The three-letter temporary symbol is derived from the first letters of these roots, which gives Ubn.

Answer: Ubn

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the species in which the central atom undergoes $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation and possesses exactly one lone pair of electrons.
questions.solution:
For $XeF_4$:
Central atom Xe has 8 valence electrons.
Number of bond pairs = 4
Number of lone pairs = $\dfrac{8 - 4}{2} = 2$
Steric number = $4 + 2 = 6$
Hybridisation is $sp^3d^2$ with 2 lone pairs.

For $BrF_5$:
Central atom Br has 7 valence electrons.
Number of bond pairs = 5
Number of lone pairs = $\dfrac{7 - 5}{2} = 1$
Steric number = $5 + 1 = 6$
Hybridisation is $sp^3d^2$ with exactly 1 lone pair.

For $PCl_5$:
Central atom P has 5 valence electrons.
Number of bond pairs = 5
Number of lone pairs = $\dfrac{5 - 5}{2} = 0$
Steric number = $5 + 0 = 5$
Hybridisation is $sp^3d$ with 0 lone pairs.

For $I_3^-$:
Central atom I has $7 + 1 = 8$ valence electrons.
Number of bond pairs = 2
Number of lone pairs = $\dfrac{8 - 2}{2} = 3$
Steric number = $2 + 3 = 5$
Hybridisation is $sp^3d$ with 3 lone pairs.

Thus, $BrF_5$ is the only species with $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation and exactly one lone pair.

Answer: $BrF_5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Formic acid (methanoic acid) exhibits certain unique and abnormal behaviors compared to other higher aliphatic carboxylic acids due to its specific structure. Which of the following statements regarding formic acid is INCORRECT?
options: It acts as a reducing agent and forms a silver mirror when treated with Tollens' reagent.
It gives a brick-red precipitate of $Cu_2O$ when heated with Fehling's solution.
It readily undergoes the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction when treated with $Cl_2$ and red phosphorus.
It rapidly dehydrates to yield carbon monoxide ($CO$) gas when heated with concentrated $H_2SO_4$.
questions.solution:
Formic acid ($H-COOH$) possesses a unique structure containing both an aldehydic group and a carboxylic acid group.

Due to the presence of the aldehydic moiety, it acts as a reducing agent. It reduces Tollens' reagent to form a silver mirror and Fehling's solution to form a brick-red precipitate of $Cu_2O$. Thus, statements (1) and (2) are correct.

Heating formic acid with concentrated $H_2SO_4$ leads to its dehydration, producing carbon monoxide ($CO$) gas and water. Thus, statement (4) is correct.

The Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction involves the halogenation of carboxylic acids at the $\alpha$-carbon. This reaction strictly requires the presence of at least one $\alpha$-hydrogen atom. Since formic acid lacks an $\alpha$-carbon atom, it does not contain any $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms and cannot undergo the HVZ reaction. Thus, statement (3) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the following chemical species,
(i) $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$
(ii) $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$
(iii) $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$
(iv) $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$
The correct decreasing order of their central bond angles is
questions.solution:
The bond angles of the given species can be determined by finding the hybridization and the number of lone pairs on the central nitrogen atom.

For $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$, the central nitrogen atom has $2$ bond pairs and $0$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp$, resulting in a linear geometry with a bond angle of $180^\circ$.

For $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$, the central nitrogen atom has $3$ bond pairs and $0$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^2$, resulting in a trigonal planar geometry with a bond angle of $120^\circ$.

For $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$, the central nitrogen atom has $2$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair. The hybridization is $sp^2$. Due to lone pair-bond pair repulsion, the bond angle is slightly less than $120^\circ$ (approximately $115^\circ$).

For $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$, the central nitrogen atom has $4$ bond pairs and $0$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^3$, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry with a bond angle of $109.5^\circ$.

Comparing the bond angles, we get $180^\circ \gt 120^\circ \gt 115^\circ \gt 109.5^\circ$.

Therefore, the decreasing order of bond angles is $\mathrm{NO_2^+} \gt \mathrm{NO_3^-} \gt \mathrm{NO_2^-} \gt \mathrm{NH_4^+}$, which corresponds to (ii) $ \gt $ (iv) $ \gt $ (i) $ \gt $ (iii).

Answer: (ii) $ \gt $ (iv) $ \gt $ (i) $ \gt $ (iii)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The given $P-V$ graph illustrates the reversible isothermal expansion of a fixed amount of an ideal gas from an initial volume $V_i$ to a final volume $V_f$ at two different constant temperatures, $T_1$ and $T_2$. Let $W_1$ and $W_2$ be the magnitudes of the work done by the gas during the expansion at temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$, respectively. Based on the graph, which of the following statements is correct?
options: $W_2  \gt  W_1$ because the area under the $P-V$ curve at $T_2$ is greater than the area under the curve at $T_1$.
$W_1  \gt  W_2$ because the gas exerts less pressure at lower temperatures, allowing for easier expansion.
$W_1 = W_2$ because the change in volume ($\Delta V = V_f - V_i$) is identical for both processes.
$W_1 = W_2$ because the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) is zero for any isothermal process of an ideal gas.
questions.solution:
The work done by a gas during a reversible expansion is given by the area under the $P-V$ curve, which is mathematically represented as $W = \int_{V_i}^{V_f} P \, dV$.

From the given graph, it is evident that the isotherm for temperature $T_2$ lies above the isotherm for temperature $T_1$. This means that for any given volume between $V_i$ and $V_f$, the pressure at $T_2$ is greater than the pressure at $T_1$.

Consequently, the area under the $P-V$ curve at $T_2$ is greater than the area under the curve at $T_1$.

Therefore, the magnitude of the work done at $T_2$ is greater than the magnitude of the work done at $T_1$, i.e., $W_2 \gt W_1$.

Answer: $W_2 \gt W_1$ because the area under the $P-V$ curve at $T_2$ is greater than the area under the curve at $T_1$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the $pH$ of a buffer solution prepared by mixing $200\text{ mL}$ of $0.05\text{ M}$ aqueous ammonia with $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.01\text{ M}$ ammonium chloride?

[Given: $pK_b$ of $NH_3 = 4.74$]
questions.solution:
Millimoles of $NH_3 = 200 \times 0.05 = 10$

Millimoles of $NH_4Cl = 100 \times 0.01 = 1$

Total volume $= 300\text{ mL}$

$[NH_3] = \dfrac{10}{300}\text{ M}$

$[NH_4^+] = \dfrac{1}{300}\text{ M}$

Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for a basic buffer:

$pOH = pK_b + \log \left( \dfrac{[NH_4^+]}{[NH_3]} \right)$

$pOH = 4.74 + \log \left( \dfrac{1/300}{10/300} \right)$

$pOH = 4.74 + \log(10^{-1}) = 4.74 - 1 = 3.74$

$pH = 14 - pOH = 14 - 3.74 = 10.26$

Answer: $10.26$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Four diatomic species are given below. Which of the following represents the correct sequence of their increasing bond length?
questions.solution:
The bond order of a diatomic species can be determined from its total number of electrons.

For $\mathrm{NO}^{+}$, the total number of electrons is $7 + 8 - 1 = 14$. Its bond order is $3$.

For $\mathrm{NO}$, the total number of electrons is $7 + 8 = 15$. Its bond order is $2.5$.

For $\mathrm{O}_2$, the total number of electrons is $8 + 8 = 16$. Its bond order is $2$.

For $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$, the total number of electrons is $8 + 8 + 1 = 17$. Its bond order is $1.5$.

Bond length is inversely proportional to bond order. Since the bond order decreases in the sequence $\mathrm{NO}^{+} \gt \mathrm{NO} \gt \mathrm{O}_2 \gt \mathrm{O}_2^{-}$, the bond length will increase in the reverse order.

Therefore, the correct sequence of increasing bond length is $\mathrm{NO}^{+} \lt \mathrm{NO} \lt \mathrm{O}_2 \lt \mathrm{O}_2^{-}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{NO}^{+} \lt \mathrm{NO} \lt \mathrm{O}_2 \lt \mathrm{O}_2^{-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the five cyclic species (I to V) shown in the figure.

According to Huckel's rule, how many of these species are aromatic?
questions.solution:
According to Huckel's rule, a species is aromatic if it is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and contains $(4n + 2)\pi$ electrons, where $n$ is an integer ($0, 1, 2, \dots$).

(I) Naphthalene: It is a planar, fully conjugated bicyclic system with $5$ double bonds, giving $10\pi$ electrons. Since $10 = 4(2) + 2$, it is aromatic.

(II) Cyclopentadienyl cation: It is a planar, fully conjugated cyclic system with $2$ double bonds, giving $4\pi$ electrons. Since $4 = 4(1)$, it is antiaromatic.

(III) Pyrrole: It is a planar, fully conjugated cyclic system. The nitrogen atom contributes its lone pair to the $\pi$ system. Total $\pi$ electrons = $4$ (from double bonds) + $2$ (from lone pair) = $6$. Since $6 = 4(1) + 2$, it is aromatic.

(IV) Cyclopropenyl anion: It is a planar, fully conjugated cyclic system. The negative charge contributes $2$ electrons to the $\pi$ system. Total $\pi$ electrons = $2$ (from double bond) + $2$ (from negative charge) = $4$. Since $4 = 4(1)$, it is antiaromatic.

(V) Thiophene: It is a planar, fully conjugated cyclic system. The sulfur atom contributes one of its lone pairs to the $\pi$ system. Total $\pi$ electrons = $4$ (from double bonds) + $2$ (from lone pair) = $6$. Since $6 = 4(1) + 2$, it is aromatic.

Therefore, the aromatic species are (I), (III), and (V). There are $3$ aromatic species in total.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Consider the organic molecule shown in the figure. A chemist attempts to determine its nitrogen content using Kjeldahl's method. Which of the following statements correctly describes the expected result?
options: The total nitrogen content will be accurately determined as both nitrogen atoms convert to $(NH_4)_2SO_4$.
Only the nitrogen atom of the $-NO_2$ group will be converted to $(NH_4)_2SO_4$, leading to an underestimation.
Only the ring nitrogen atom will be converted to $(NH_4)_2SO_4$, leading to an underestimation.
The method will fail completely because neither the ring nitrogen nor the nitro nitrogen converts to $(NH_4)_2SO_4$.
questions.solution:
Kjeldahl's method is used for the quantitative estimation of nitrogen in organic compounds. In this method, the organic compound is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid, which converts the nitrogen present in the compound to ammonium sulfate, $(NH_4)_2SO_4$.

However, Kjeldahl's method has specific limitations. It is not applicable to compounds containing nitrogen in:
1. Nitro groups ($-NO_2$)
2. Azo groups ($-N=N-$)
3. Aromatic rings (e.g., pyridine, quinoline)

In these types of compounds, the nitrogen atoms are not quantitatively converted to ammonium sulfate under the standard digestion conditions.

The given molecule is 3-nitropyridine, which contains both a nitro group and a nitrogen atom within an aromatic ring (pyridine ring). Since both nitrogen atoms fall under the exceptions for Kjeldahl's method, neither will be converted to $(NH_4)_2SO_4$. Therefore, the method will fail completely for this compound.

Answer: The method will fail completely because neither the ring nitrogen nor the nitro nitrogen converts to $(NH_4)_2SO_4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What mass of glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) must be dissolved in $500\text{ g}$ of water to prepare a $0.2\text{ m}$ aqueous solution?
(Molar mass of glucose = $180\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Molality is defined as the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent.

$m = \dfrac{w \times 1000}{M \times W}$

Where $w$ is the mass of solute, $M$ is the molar mass of solute, and $W$ is the mass of solvent in grams.

Substituting the given values:

$0.2 = \dfrac{w \times 1000}{180 \times 500}$

$0.2 = \dfrac{w \times 2}{180}$

$0.2 = \dfrac{w}{90}$

$w = 18\text{ g}$

Answer: $18\text{ g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The given graph represents the kinetics of a reaction, showing a straight line passing through the origin.

The $y$ and $x$ axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively, can be correctly identified as:
options: zero order ($y = \text{rate}$, $x = \text{concentration}$), first order ($y = t_{1/2}$, $x = \text{initial concentration}$)
zero order ($y = t_{1/2}$, $x = \text{initial concentration}$), first order ($y = \text{rate}$, $x = \text{concentration}$)
questions.solution:
The given graph is a straight line passing through the origin, which represents an equation of the form $y = mx$.

For a zero-order reaction, the half-life is given by:
$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2k}$
If we plot $y = t_{1/2}$ against $x = [A]_0$ (initial concentration), we get a straight line passing through the origin with a slope of $\dfrac{1}{2k}$.

For a first-order reaction, the rate law is given by:
$\text{Rate} = k[A]$
If we plot $y = \text{Rate}$ against $x = [A]$ (concentration), we get a straight line passing through the origin with a slope of $k$.

Let us check the other options:
In option (A), for a zero-order reaction, rate is independent of concentration, so the graph of rate vs concentration would be a horizontal line.
In option (C), for a zero-order reaction, $[A] = [A]_0 - kt$, which gives a straight line with a negative slope, not passing through the origin.
In option (D), for a zero-order reaction, rate is constant over time, giving a horizontal line.

Therefore, only option (B) correctly represents the axes for both zero and first-order reactions that yield the given graph.

Answer: zero order ($y = t_{1/2}$, $x = \text{initial concentration}$), first order ($y = \text{rate}$, $x = \text{concentration}$)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : The oxygen-oxygen bond length in peroxide ion ($O_2^{2-}$) is greater than that in superoxide ion ($O_2^-$).
Reason : The bond order of peroxide ion is lower than that of superoxide ion.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
The number of electrons in superoxide ion $O_2^-$ is $17$.

The molecular orbital electronic configuration of $O_2^-$ is $\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_y}^1$.

Bond order of $O_2^- = \dfrac{10 - 7}{2} = 1.5$.

The number of electrons in peroxide ion $O_2^{2-}$ is $18$.

The molecular orbital electronic configuration of $O_2^{2-}$ is $\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_y}^2$.

Bond order of $O_2^{2-} = \dfrac{10 - 8}{2} = 1$.

Since bond length is inversely proportional to bond order, the oxygen-oxygen bond length in peroxide ion is greater than that in superoxide ion.

Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

Answer: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The third ionisation enthalpy of Lutetium (Lu) is anomalously low. This is primarily attributed to:
options: its exceptionally small atomic radius due to lanthanoid contraction
the attainment of a highly stable completely filled $4f^{14}$ configuration
the strong shielding effect provided by the inner $5d$ electrons
its high electronegativity compared to the early lanthanoids
questions.solution:
The atomic number of Lutetium (Lu) is $71$.

The electronic configuration of Lu is $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^{1} 6s^{2}$.

During the first and second ionisations, the two $6s$ electrons are removed, forming $\text{Lu}^{2+}$ with the configuration $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^{1}$.

The third ionisation involves the removal of the single $5d$ electron. This results in the formation of $\text{Lu}^{3+}$ with the configuration $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14}$.

Since the resulting $4f^{14}$ configuration is completely filled and highly stable, the removal of the third electron requires less energy. Thus, the third ionisation enthalpy of Lu is anomalously low.

Answer: the attainment of a highly stable completely filled $4f^{14}$ configuration

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The figure below shows four different substituted aryl halides labeled P, Q, R, and S.

These compounds undergo nucleophilic aromatic substitution when heated with aqueous NaOH. The reaction proceeds via an addition-elimination mechanism involving a carbanion intermediate. Identify the correct decreasing order of reactivity for these compounds towards this reaction.
questions.solution:
Nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($S_{N}Ar$) proceeds via an addition-elimination mechanism, forming a carbanion intermediate (Meisenheimer complex) in the rate-determining step.

The reactivity of aryl halides towards $S_{N}Ar$ increases with the presence of electron-withdrawing groups (EWGs) at the ortho and para positions, as they stabilize the carbanion intermediate through $-I$ and $-M$ effects. Conversely, electron-donating groups (EDGs) destabilize the intermediate and decrease reactivity.

Analyzing the given compounds:
Compound Q (1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene) has two strong EWGs ($-NO_2$) at ortho and para positions, providing maximum stabilization to the intermediate. Thus, it is the most reactive.
Compound S (1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene) has one $-NO_2$ group at the para position, making it more reactive than unsubstituted chlorobenzene.
Compound P (chlorobenzene) has no substituents on the ring.
Compound R (1-chloro-4-methoxybenzene) has an $-OCH_3$ group at the para position. The $-OCH_3$ group is an EDG due to its strong $+M$ effect, which destabilizes the carbanion intermediate, making it the least reactive.

Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity is Q > S > P > R.

Answer: Q > S > P > R

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkyl chloride $\text{'X'}$ reacts with magnesium metal in dry ether to form a Grignard reagent. This Grignard reagent is then treated with solid carbon dioxide, followed by acid hydrolysis, to yield $2$-methylpropanoic acid. Identify the alkyl chloride $\text{'X'}$.
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alkyl chloride $X$ ($R-Cl$) with magnesium in dry ether forms a Grignard reagent $RMgCl$.

$R-Cl + Mg \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} RMgCl$

The Grignard reagent reacts with solid $CO_2$ followed by acid hydrolysis to form a carboxylic acid $RCOOH$.

$RMgCl + CO_2 \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} RCOOH$

The product is given as $2$-methylpropanoic acid, which has the structure $(CH_3)_2CH-COOH$.

Comparing $RCOOH$ with $(CH_3)_2CH-COOH$, the alkyl group $R$ is the isopropyl group, $(CH_3)_2CH-$.

Therefore, the alkyl chloride $X$ is isopropyl chloride, which is $2$-chloropropane, $(CH_3)_2CH-Cl$.

Answer: $2$-Chloropropane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the correct decreasing order of reactivity of the following alkyl halides towards sodium methoxide in a Williamson synthesis?

I. $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3}$
II. $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-Br}$
III. $\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-Br}$
IV. $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-Br}$
questions.solution:
Williamson ether synthesis proceeds via an $S_N2$ mechanism.

The rate of an $S_N2$ reaction is inversely proportional to the steric hindrance around the electrophilic carbon and is enhanced by the stabilization of the transition state.

Compound III ($\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-Br}$) is a benzylic halide. Its $S_N2$ transition state is highly stabilized by the adjacent phenyl ring through conjugation, making it the most reactive.

Compound IV ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-Br}$) is an unbranched primary alkyl halide with minimal steric hindrance.

Compound II ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-Br}$) is a primary alkyl halide but has a methyl group at the $\beta$-position. This branching increases steric hindrance, making it less reactive than IV.

Compound I ($\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3}$) is a secondary alkyl halide, which is more sterically hindered at the $\alpha$-carbon than primary alkyl halides, making it the least reactive.

Therefore, the decreasing order of reactivity is III $ \gt $ IV $ \gt $ II $ \gt $ I.

Answer: III $ \gt $ IV $ \gt $ II $ \gt $ I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$20 \text{ mL}$ of liquid pyridine ($C_5H_5N$, specific gravity $0.79$) is completely burnt in excess oxygen. Find the total volume of the gaseous products measured at STP.
(Assume water formed is in the liquid state and molar volume of a gas at STP is $22.4 \text{ L}$)
questions.solution:
Mass of pyridine ($C_5H_5N$) $= \text{Volume} \times \text{Density} = 20 \times 0.79 = 15.8 \text{ g}$

Molar mass of $C_5H_5N = (5 \times 12) + (5 \times 1) + 14 = 79 \text{ g/mol}$

Moles of pyridine $= \dfrac{15.8}{79} = 0.2 \text{ mol}$

The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of pyridine is:
$C_5H_5N(l) + \dfrac{25}{4} O_2(g) \rightarrow 5 CO_2(g) + \dfrac{5}{2} H_2O(l) + \dfrac{1}{2} N_2(g)$

Since water is in the liquid state, the gaseous products are $CO_2$ and $N_2$.

Moles of gaseous products per mole of pyridine $= 5 + \dfrac{1}{2} = 5.5 \text{ mol}$

Total moles of gaseous products formed $= 0.2 \times 5.5 = 1.1 \text{ mol}$

Volume of gaseous products at STP $= 1.1 \times 22.4 \text{ L} = 24.64 \text{ L}$

Answer: $24.64 \text{ L}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Carbohydrates are classified into three major groups on the basis of their behavior towards hydrolysis. Which of the following statements regarding this classification is incorrect?
options: Monosaccharides cannot be hydrolysed further to give simpler units of polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones.
Carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units on hydrolysis are called oligosaccharides.
Polysaccharides yield a large number of monosaccharide units on hydrolysis and are generally sweet in taste.
Sucrose, maltose, and lactose are common examples of oligosaccharides.
questions.solution:
Carbohydrates are classified into monosaccharides, oligosaccharides, and polysaccharides based on their hydrolysis behavior.

Monosaccharides are the simplest carbohydrates and cannot be hydrolysed further into simpler units of polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones.

Oligosaccharides yield two to ten monosaccharide units on hydrolysis. Common examples include sucrose, maltose, and lactose, which are disaccharides.

Polysaccharides yield a large number of monosaccharide units on hydrolysis. However, unlike monosaccharides and oligosaccharides, polysaccharides are generally not sweet in taste and are therefore referred to as non-sugars. Examples include starch, cellulose, and glycogen.

Thus, the statement claiming that polysaccharides are generally sweet in taste is incorrect.

Answer: Polysaccharides yield a large number of monosaccharide units on hydrolysis and are generally sweet in taste.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a $\text{He}^+$ ion, the distance of the electron from the nucleus in the third Bohr orbit is $238.05\text{ pm}$. What will be the corresponding distance for an electron revolving in the fifth Bohr orbit of a $\text{B}^{4+}$ ion?
questions.solution:
The radius of the $n$-th Bohr orbit for a hydrogen-like species is given by:

$r_n = r_0 \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$

For the $\text{He}^+$ ion ($Z = 2$) in the third orbit ($n = 3$):

$r_{\text{He}^+} = r_0 \dfrac{3^2}{2} = 238.05\text{ pm}$

$r_0 = \dfrac{238.05 \times 2}{9} = 52.9\text{ pm}$

For the $\text{B}^{4+}$ ion ($Z = 5$) in the fifth orbit ($n = 5$):

$r_{\text{B}^{4+}} = r_0 \dfrac{5^2}{5} = 5 r_0$

Substituting the value of $r_0$:

$r_{\text{B}^{4+}} = 5 \times 52.9 = 264.5\text{ pm}$

Answer: $264.5\text{ pm}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct IUPAC name for the given organic compound.
questions.solution:
According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the principal functional group is the ketone ($-C=O$), which must receive the lowest possible locant.

The longest carbon chain containing the ketone group has $7$ carbon atoms, so the parent chain is heptane.

Numbering the chain from left to right places the ketone at position $3$. Numbering from right to left places it at position $5$. Therefore, the correct numbering is from left to right.

The substituents and their positions are:
- A chloro group at C-$2$
- A methyl group at C-$4$
- A bromo group at C-$6$

The substituents must be listed in alphabetical order: bromo, chloro, methyl.

Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is $6$-bromo-$2$-chloro-$4$-methylheptan-$3$-one.

Answer: $6$-bromo-$2$-chloro-$4$-methylheptan-$3$-one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion (A): In a first-order reaction, the time required to reduce the reactant concentration from $0.8 \text{ M}$ to $0.4 \text{ M}$ is exactly the same as the time required to reduce it from $0.4 \text{ M}$ to $0.2 \text{ M}$.
Reason (R): The half-life of a first-order reaction is given by $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}$, which is independent of the initial concentration.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, the time required to reduce the concentration of the reactant to half of its initial value is called the half-life, denoted by $t_{1/2}$.

The reduction from $0.8 \text{ M}$ to $0.4 \text{ M}$ represents one half-life. Similarly, the reduction from $0.4 \text{ M}$ to $0.2 \text{ M}$ also represents one half-life.

The half-life of a first-order reaction is given by the expression $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}$.

This expression shows that the half-life is independent of the initial concentration of the reactant. Therefore, the time taken for both reductions is exactly the same.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : The oxygen molecule ($O_2$) is attracted by an external magnetic field.
Reason : According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the $O_2$ molecule possesses two unpaired electrons in its degenerate $\pi^*$ antibonding orbitals.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of $O_2$ molecule (16 electrons) according to Molecular Orbital Theory is:

$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 = \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^{*1} = \pi_{2p_y}^{*1}$

Due to the presence of two unpaired electrons in the degenerate $\pi^{*}$ antibonding orbitals, the $O_2$ molecule is paramagnetic in nature.

Paramagnetic substances are attracted by an external magnetic field.

Thus, both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For a galvanic cell operating at $298\text{ K}$, the overall cell reaction is given as:

$2\text{Al(s)} + 3\text{Cu}^{2+}(0.001\text{ M}) \rightarrow 2\text{Al}^{3+}(0.001\text{ M}) + 3\text{Cu(s)}$

If the standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$) for this reaction is $2.00\text{ V}$, what is the operating electromotive force (emf) of the cell?
(Assume $\dfrac{2.303 RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}$ at $298\text{ K}$)
questions.solution:
The given cell reaction is:

$2\text{Al(s)} + 3\text{Cu}^{2+}(0.001\text{ M}) \rightarrow 2\text{Al}^{3+}(0.001\text{ M}) + 3\text{Cu(s)}$

The number of electrons transferred in the balanced reaction is $n = 6$.

The reaction quotient $Q$ is given by:

$Q = \dfrac{[\text{Al}^{3+}]^2}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]^3}$

Substituting the given concentrations:

$Q = \dfrac{(10^{-3})^2}{(10^{-3})^3} = \dfrac{10^{-6}}{10^{-9}} = 10^3$

Using the Nernst equation:

$E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \dfrac{0.059}{n} \log Q$

Substituting the values:

$E_{\text{cell}} = 2.00 - \dfrac{0.059}{6} \log(10^3)$

$E_{\text{cell}} = 2.00 - \dfrac{0.059}{6} \times 3$

$E_{\text{cell}} = 2.00 - \dfrac{0.059}{2}$

$E_{\text{cell}} = 2.00 - 0.0295 = 1.9705\text{ V}$

Answer: $1.9705\text{ V}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first-order reaction has an initial reactant concentration of $0.5\text{ mol L}^{-1}$. After exactly $30\text{ s}$, the concentration is found to be $5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}$. The rate constant for this reaction is:
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}$

Given:
$[A]_0 = 0.5\text{ mol L}^{-1}$
$[A]_t = 5 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}$
$t = 30\text{ s}$

Substituting the values:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{30} \log \left( \dfrac{0.5}{5 \times 10^{-4}} \right)$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{30} \log (10^3)$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{30} \times 3$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{10} = 0.2303\text{ s}^{-1}$

Answer: $0.2303\text{ s}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the organic molecule provided in the figure. It is subjected to the following reaction sequence:

1. $LiAlH_4$ in ether, followed by $H_2O$
2. $NaNO_2$ and $HCl$ at $273-278$ K
3. Warming with $H_2O$

Identify the major organic product formed at the end of this sequence.
questions.solution:
The given starting material is pentanamide, which has a 5-carbon chain: $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CONH_2$.

Reaction with $LiAlH_4$ in ether followed by $H_2O$ reduces the amide to a primary amine. The carbonyl group ($-C=O$) is converted to a methylene group ($-CH_2-$).
$CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CONH_2 \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4} CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_2NH_2$

Reaction of the resulting primary aliphatic amine (pentan-1-amine) with $NaNO_2$ and $HCl$ at $273-278$ K generates nitrous acid ($HNO_2$), which forms an unstable aliphatic diazonium salt.
$CH_3(CH_2)_4NH_2 \xrightarrow{NaNO_2, HCl} [CH_3(CH_2)_4N_2^+Cl^-]$

Warming this diazonium salt with water causes it to decompose, releasing nitrogen gas and forming the corresponding primary alcohol.
$[CH_3(CH_2)_4N_2^+Cl^-] \xrightarrow{H_2O, \Delta} CH_3(CH_2)_4OH + N_2 + HCl$

The final major organic product is pentan-1-ol.

Answer: Pentan-1-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An alkene X upon reductive ozonolysis ($O_3$, followed by $Zn/H_2O$) yields a mixture of two isomeric ketones, Y and Z. It is observed that both Y and Z respond positively to the iodoform test. Which of the following is the correct IUPAC name of the alkene X?
questions.solution:
Reductive ozonolysis of an alkene cleaves the carbon-carbon double bond to form carbonyl compounds.

Since the products Y and Z are both ketones, the original alkene X must be a tetrasubstituted alkene. For both ketones to respond positively to the iodoform test, they must be methyl ketones, meaning each must contain a $CH_3-CO-$ group.

Furthermore, Y and Z are isomeric, which means they must possess the same molecular formula.

Evaluating the ozonolysis products for each given option:

For 2,3-dimethylhex-2-ene, the structure is $CH_3-C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$. Its ozonolysis yields propan-2-one ($C_3H_6O$) and pentan-2-one ($C_5H_{10}O$). These products are not isomers.

For 2,3,4-trimethylhept-3-ene, the structure is $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$. Its ozonolysis yields 3-methylbutan-2-one ($C_5H_{10}O$) and pentan-2-one ($C_5H_{10}O$). Both are methyl ketones and have the same molecular formula, making them isomers. This satisfies all given conditions.

For 2,4-dimethylhex-3-ene, the structure is $CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH=C(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$. Its ozonolysis yields 2-methylpropanal (an aldehyde) and butan-2-one. This does not result in a mixture of two ketones.

For 2,3,5-trimethylhex-2-ene, the structure is $CH_3-C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$. Its ozonolysis yields propan-2-one ($C_3H_6O$) and 4-methylpentan-2-one ($C_6H_{12}O$). These products are not isomers.

Therefore, the correct IUPAC name of the alkene is 2,3,4-trimethylhept-3-ene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone shown below is formed as one of the products in a cross-aldol condensation reaction followed by heating.

Identify the pair of reactants that will produce this compound.
questions.solution:
To identify the reactants that produce the given $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone, we can perform a retro-aldol analysis by cleaving the carbon-carbon double bond.

The structure of the given compound is $CH_3-CH_2-C(=O)-CH=C(CH_3)_2$.

In an aldol condensation, the double bond is formed between the $\alpha$-carbon of the enolate (nucleophile) and the carbonyl carbon ($\beta$-carbon in the product) of the other reactant (electrophile).

Cleaving the $C_{\alpha}=C_{\beta}$ double bond:
1. The $\alpha$-carbon (the $-CH=$ group adjacent to the carbonyl) gains two hydrogen atoms to form the original ketone. This gives $CH_3-CH_2-C(=O)-CH_3$, which is butan-2-one.
2. The $\beta$-carbon (the $=C(CH_3)_2$ group) gains an oxygen atom to form the original carbonyl compound. This gives $O=C(CH_3)_2$, which is propanone (acetone).

Thus, the cross-aldol condensation between butan-2-one (acting as the enolate at the terminal methyl group) and propanone yields the given product.

Answer: Butan-2-one and propanone

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the taxonomic hierarchy for a plant, moving from the most specific to the most general category?
options: Species \rightarrow  Genus \rightarrow  Family \rightarrow  Class \rightarrow  Order \rightarrow  Division \rightarrow  Kingdom
Species \rightarrow  Genus \rightarrow  Family \rightarrow  Order \rightarrow  Class \rightarrow  Division \rightarrow  Kingdom
Species \rightarrow  Genus \rightarrow  Order \rightarrow  Family \rightarrow  Class \rightarrow  Phylum \rightarrow  Kingdom
Species \rightarrow  Genus \rightarrow  Family \rightarrow  Order \rightarrow  Class \rightarrow  Phylum \rightarrow  Kingdom
questions.solution:
The taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of various taxonomic categories in a definite order.

Moving from the most specific (lowest) to the most general (highest) category, the standard sequence is:
Species \rightarrow Genus \rightarrow Family \rightarrow Order \rightarrow Class \rightarrow Phylum/Division \rightarrow Kingdom.

In the case of plants, the term 'Division' is used instead of 'Phylum'.

Therefore, the correct sequence for a plant is:
Species \rightarrow Genus \rightarrow Family \rightarrow Order \rightarrow Class \rightarrow Division \rightarrow Kingdom.

Answer: Species \rightarrow Genus \rightarrow Family \rightarrow Order \rightarrow Class \rightarrow Division \rightarrow Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Agar, a commercial product extensively used to grow microbes and in the preparation of ice-creams and jellies, is obtained from which of the following pairs of algae?
questions.solution:
Agar is a commercial product obtained from red algae (Rhodophyceae), specifically from the genera $Gelidium$ and $Gracilaria$.

It is extensively used as a solidifying agent in culture media to grow microbes and in the food industry for the preparation of ice-creams and jellies.

$Laminaria$ and $Sargassum$ are brown algae that produce algin.

$Chlorella$ and $Spirulina$ are unicellular organisms rich in proteins and are used as food supplements.

Answer: $Gelidium$ and $Gracilaria$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of alga and its characteristic reserve food or pigment is correctly matched?
questions.solution:
Fucus is a brown alga (Phaeophyceae) which contains the pigment fucoxanthin and stores food as mannitol and laminarin. Phycoerythrin is a characteristic pigment of red algae.

Polysiphonia is a red alga (Rhodophyceae) which stores food as floridean starch, not mannitol.

Dictyota is a brown alga (Phaeophyceae) and its characteristic pigment is fucoxanthin. This pair is correctly matched.

Chara is a green alga (Chlorophyceae) which stores food as starch, whereas laminarin is the reserve food of brown algae.

Answer: Dictyota - Fucoxanthin

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Identify the plants that possess actinomorphic flowers :
(a) Bean
(b) Mustard
(c) Canna
(d) Datura
(e) Chilli

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Actinomorphic flowers possess radial symmetry, meaning they can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the center.

Mustard, Datura, and Chilli have actinomorphic flowers.

Bean has zygomorphic flowers (bilateral symmetry), which can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane.

Canna has asymmetric (irregular) flowers, which cannot be divided into two similar halves by any vertical plane passing through the center.

Therefore, the plants possessing actinomorphic flowers are Mustard, Datura, and Chilli.

Answer: (b), (d), (e) Only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The beginning of which stage of prophase I is recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers?
questions.solution:
During prophase I of meiosis, the beginning of the diplotene stage is characterized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex.

The recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents tend to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers. These X-shaped structures formed during separation are called chiasmata.

Answer: Diplotene

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The plant growth regulator that is widely known to act as an antagonist to gibberellic acid is primarily responsible for:
options: promoting nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence.
stimulating the closure of stomata in the epidermis.
increasing the length of the grape stalks.
questions.solution:
The plant growth regulator that acts as an antagonist to gibberellic acid is abscisic acid (ABA).

Abscisic acid is widely known as a stress hormone as it increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of environmental stresses.

A major function of abscisic acid is to stimulate the closure of stomata in the epidermis, thereby preventing water loss during water stress conditions.

Initiating rooting in stem cuttings is a function of auxins.

Promoting nutrient mobilisation which helps in the delay of leaf senescence is a function of cytokinins.

Increasing the length of grape stalks is a function of gibberellins.

Answer: stimulating the closure of stomata in the epidermis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The given figure represents the typical growth curve of a plant organ growing in a natural environment. Which of the following statements correctly identifies the characteristic of the phase labelled 'Q'?
options: It is the lag phase where the rate of growth is initially very slow.
It is the stationary phase where growth slows down due to a limited nutrient supply.
