It is the exponential phase where both progeny cells following mitotic division retain the ability to divide.
It represents a phase of arithmetic growth where only one daughter cell continues to divide.
questions.solution:
The given figure represents a typical sigmoid growth curve, which is characteristic of living organisms growing in a natural environment.

The curve is divided into three main phases:
1. Phase P (Lag phase): The initial phase where the rate of growth is very slow.
2. Phase Q (Log or Exponential phase): The phase of maximum and rapid growth. During this phase, growth is geometric, meaning both progeny cells formed after mitotic cell division retain the ability to divide and continue to do so.
3. Phase R (Stationary phase): The final phase where growth slows down and eventually stops due to the depletion of nutrients and limited resources.

Therefore, phase 'Q' represents the exponential phase where both daughter cells continue to divide.

Answer: It is the exponential phase where both progeny cells following mitotic division retain the ability to divide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During the terminal stages of aerobic respiration, a proton gradient is established across the inner mitochondrial membrane. Which enzyme complex utilizes this gradient to catalyze the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate?
questions.solution:
During the terminal stages of aerobic respiration, the electron transport chain pumps protons from the mitochondrial matrix into the intermembrane space, creating a proton gradient.

This proton gradient generates a proton motive force. The enzyme complex ATP synthase (Complex V) utilizes this proton gradient to catalyze the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate ($P_i$) as protons flow back into the matrix through its $F_0$ channel.

Answer: ATP synthase

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Under high light intensities, if the ambient $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration is gradually increased from $380 \mu \mathrm{L} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$ to $430 \mu \mathrm{L} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$, which of the following plants will exhibit a continuous increase in its rate of photosynthesis?
questions.solution:
Sugarcane, Maize, and Sorghum are $C_4$ plants, whereas Tomato is a $C_3$ plant.

$C_4$ plants show saturation in the rate of photosynthesis at about $360 \mu \mathrm{L} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2$. Therefore, increasing the $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration from $380 \mu \mathrm{L} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$ to $430 \mu \mathrm{L} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$ will not increase their photosynthetic rate, as they are already saturated.

$C_3$ plants respond to increased $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration and show saturation only beyond $450 \mu \mathrm{L} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$. Thus, as the $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration is gradually increased from $380 \mu \mathrm{L} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$ to $430 \mu \mathrm{L} \mathrm{L}^{-1}$, a $C_3$ plant like Tomato will exhibit a continuous increase in its rate of photosynthesis.

Answer: Tomato

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: According to the chromosomal basis of sex determination, which of the following statements accurately describes the gametes produced by a male in the XX-XO system?
options: 50% of the sperms carry an X chromosome and 50% carry a Y chromosome.
100% of the sperms carry a single X chromosome.
50% of the sperms carry an X chromosome and 50% lack any sex chromosome.
50% of the sperms carry a Z chromosome and 50% carry a W chromosome.
questions.solution:
In the XX-XO type of sex determination, females are homogametic (XX) and males are heterogametic (XO).

Males possess only one X chromosome besides the autosomes.

During spermatogenesis, 50% of the sperms receive the X chromosome, while the remaining 50% do not receive any sex chromosome.

Therefore, 50% of the sperms carry an X chromosome and 50% lack any sex chromosome.

Answer: 50% of the sperms carry an X chromosome and 50% lack any sex chromosome.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a typical biogas plant, methanogens grow anaerobically on cellulosic materials present in cow dung. Which of the following represents the correct combination of gases primarily produced by these bacteria during this process?
options: Carbon dioxide, Nitrogen, and Hydrogen sulphide
questions.solution:
In a biogas plant, certain bacteria grow anaerobically on cellulosic material present in cow dung to produce a large amount of methane along with carbon dioxide and hydrogen. These bacteria are collectively called methanogens, with Methanobacterium being a common example.

The mixture of gases produced is called biogas, which predominantly consists of methane ($CH_4$), carbon dioxide ($CO_2$), and hydrogen ($H_2$).

Answer: Methane, Carbon dioxide, and Hydrogen

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Read the following conservation strategies:
I. Seed banks
II. Sacred groves
III. Botanical gardens
IV. Biosphere reserves

Which of the above are considered ex situ conservation methods?
questions.solution:
Conservation strategies are broadly classified into in situ (on-site) and ex situ (off-site) conservation.

Ex situ conservation involves protecting endangered species of plants and animals outside their natural habitats. Examples include botanical gardens, zoological parks, wildlife safari parks, seed banks, and cryopreservation techniques.

In situ conservation involves protecting species in their natural habitats. Examples include national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, and sacred groves.

From the given list:
I. Seed banks \rightarrow Ex situ
II. Sacred groves \rightarrow In situ
III. Botanical gardens \rightarrow Ex situ
IV. Biosphere reserves \rightarrow In situ

Therefore, I and III are considered ex situ conservation methods.

Answer: I and III only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Read the following anatomical features:

i) Presence of unicellular root hairs

ii) Endodermis with Casparian strips

iii) Large and well-developed pith

iv) Two to four xylem patches

v) Initiation of lateral roots from the pericycle

vi) Polyarch condition of vascular bundles

vii) Endarch arrangement of primary xylem

viii) Parenchymatous conjunctive tissue

Which of the above features are characteristic of a typical dicotyledonous root?
questions.solution:
The anatomical features of a typical dicotyledonous root are as follows:

i) Presence of unicellular root hairs: The outermost layer is epiblema, which bears unicellular root hairs.

ii) Endodermis with Casparian strips: The endodermis consists of barrel-shaped cells with water-impermeable, waxy suberin deposition in the form of Casparian strips.

iii) Large and well-developed pith: This is a feature of monocot roots. In dicot roots, the pith is small or inconspicuous.

iv) Two to four xylem patches: Dicot roots typically exhibit a diarch to tetrarch condition (2 to 4 xylem and phloem patches).

v) Initiation of lateral roots from the pericycle: The pericycle gives rise to lateral roots and vascular cambium during secondary growth.

vi) Polyarch condition of vascular bundles: This is characteristic of monocot roots, which have more than six xylem bundles.

vii) Endarch arrangement of primary xylem: Roots have an exarch arrangement (protoxylem towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the centre). Endarch arrangement is found in stems.

viii) Parenchymatous conjunctive tissue: The parenchymatous cells lying between the xylem and phloem patches are called conjunctive tissue.

Therefore, the correct features for a dicotyledonous root are i, ii, iv, v, and viii.

Answer: i, ii, iv, v, viii

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following respiratory substrates yields a Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of approximately $0.9$ during aerobic respiration?
questions.solution:
The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) is defined as the ratio of the volume of $CO_2$ evolved to the volume of $O_2$ consumed during respiration.

For carbohydrates like glucose, the RQ is $1.0$.

For fats and fatty acids, the RQ is less than $1$, typically around $0.7$.

For proteins, the RQ is approximately $0.9$.

For organic acids like malic acid, the RQ is greater than $1$ (approximately $1.33$).

Therefore, proteins yield a Respiratory Quotient of approximately $0.9$.

Answer: Proteins

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The given figure illustrates a strawberry. Which of the following statements correctly describes the labelled parts 'X' or 'Y'?
options: Structure 'X' is the fleshy mesocarp, which classifies this as a true fruit.
Structure 'X' is the enlarged thalamus, which classifies this as a false fruit.
Structure 'Y' is a parthenocarpic seed developed without fertilization.
Structure 'Y' is the endocarp that protects the developing embryo.
questions.solution:
Based on the provided image of a strawberry:

1. The strawberry is an example of a false fruit (pseudocarp). In true fruits, the fruit develops solely from the ovary. However, in false fruits, other floral parts also contribute to fruit formation.

2. In the case of a strawberry, the fleshy, edible part labelled 'X' is the enlarged receptacle or thalamus.

3. The small, seed-like structures on the surface, labelled 'Y', are actually the true fruits, known botanically as achenes. Each achene contains a single seed.

Therefore, structure 'X' is the enlarged thalamus, which classifies the strawberry as a false fruit.

Answer: Structure 'X' is the enlarged thalamus, which classifies this as a false fruit.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the process of RNA interference (RNAi) utilized to develop nematode-resistant plants, the source of the complementary RNA could be:
options: Mobile genetic elements that replicate via an RNA intermediate
Selectable marker genes such as $amp^{R}$ or $tet^{R}$
T-DNA from the Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens
questions.solution:
RNA interference (RNAi) is a method of cellular defense present in all eukaryotic organisms. It involves the silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary dsRNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of the mRNA.

The source of this complementary RNA could be from an infection by viruses having RNA genomes or mobile genetic elements (transposons) that replicate via an RNA intermediate.

Therefore, mobile genetic elements that replicate via an RNA intermediate serve as a source of complementary RNA in the process of RNA interference.

Answer: Mobile genetic elements that replicate via an RNA intermediate

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Smack, a drug that acts as a depressant and slows down body functions, is chemically obtained by the acetylation of a compound extracted from the latex of:
questions.solution:
Smack, also known as heroin, is chemically diacetylmorphine. It is obtained by the acetylation of morphine.

Morphine is extracted from the latex of the poppy plant, Papaver somniferum.

Therefore, the compound is extracted from the latex of Papaver somniferum.

Answer: Papaver somniferum

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Earthworms feed on fragmented plant remains and soil organic matter in an agricultural field. Ecologically, they are participating in which of the following pathways of energy flow?
options: Grazing food chain as primary producers
Parasitic food chain as primary consumers
Grazing food chain as secondary consumers
questions.solution:
Earthworms feed on dead and decaying organic matter, such as fragmented plant remains and soil organic matter, which is known as detritus.

Organisms that feed on detritus are called detritivores. By breaking down this organic matter, they play a crucial role in the detritus food chain, facilitating the recycling of nutrients back into the ecosystem.

Therefore, earthworms participate in the detritus food chain as detritivores.

Answer: Detritus food chain as detritivores

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In members of phylum Arthropoda, the process of excretion primarily takes place through which of the following structures?
questions.solution:
In members of phylum Arthropoda, excretion primarily takes place through Malpighian tubules.

Flame cells are the excretory structures in Platyhelminthes.

Nephridia are the excretory structures in Annelida.

Proboscis gland is the excretory structure in Hemichordata.

Answer: Malpighian tubules

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In which of the following groups of animals is the body covered by dry and cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes?
questions.solution:
The presence of dry and cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes is a characteristic feature of the class Reptilia.

Let us evaluate the given options:

Option (A): Testudo (Reptile), Neophron (Aves), Macropus (Mammal).

Option (B): Salamandra (Amphibian), Hemidactylus (Reptile), Pteropus (Mammal).

Option (C): Chelone (Reptile), Calotes (Reptile), Naja (Reptile). All three belong to the class Reptilia.

Option (D): Bangarus (Reptile), Columba (Aves), Crocodilus (Reptile).

Therefore, the group containing only reptiles is Chelone, Calotes, and Naja.

Answer: Chelone, Calotes, Naja

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When three molecules of a hexose sugar ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) are joined together by glycosidic bonds to form a trisaccharide, water molecules are eliminated during the condensation process. What will be the molecular formula of the resulting trisaccharide?
questions.solution:
Three molecules of hexose sugar ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) undergo condensation to form a trisaccharide.

During the formation of a trisaccharide from three monosaccharides, two glycosidic bonds are formed.

Each glycosidic bond formation results in the elimination of one water molecule ($H_2O$). Thus, two water molecules ($2H_2O$) are eliminated in total.

Total atoms before condensation: $3 \times C_6H_{12}O_6 = C_{18}H_{36}O_{18}$

Atoms eliminated: $2 \times H_2O = H_4O_2$

Molecular formula of the trisaccharide: $C_{18}H_{36}O_{18} - H_4O_2 = C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}$

Answer: $C_{18}H_{32}O_{16}$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Ammonia is generally excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or through gill surfaces as ammonium ions. Which of the following organisms primarily exhibits this mode of nitrogenous waste excretion?
questions.solution:
Ammonia is the most toxic form of nitrogenous waste and requires large amounts of water for its elimination. Organisms that excrete ammonia are called ammonotelic.

Many bony fishes, aquatic amphibians, and aquatic insects are ammonotelic in nature. Ammonia, being readily soluble, is generally excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or through gill surfaces (in fishes) as ammonium ions.

Among the given options:
Catla is a bony fish and is ammonotelic.
Scoliodon is a cartilaginous fish and is ureotelic.
Testudo is a reptile and is uricotelic.
Delphinus is an aquatic mammal and is ureotelic.

Answer: Catla

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The human respiratory system is functionally divided into a conducting part and a respiratory (exchange) part. Which of the following correctly identifies the structures forming the exchange part and their primary function?
options: External nostrils to terminal bronchioles; humidifies and warms the inhaled air
Alveoli and their ducts; site of actual diffusion of $\text{O}_{2}$ and $\text{CO}_{2}$ between blood and atmospheric air
Trachea, bronchi, and initial bronchioles; clears inhaled air from foreign particles
Terminal bronchioles and alveoli; brings the temperature of inhaled air to body temperature
questions.solution:
The human respiratory system consists of a conducting part and a respiratory or exchange part.

The conducting part starts from the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles. Its functions include transporting atmospheric air to the alveoli, clearing it from foreign particles, humidifying the air, and bringing it to body temperature.

The exchange part comprises the alveoli and their ducts. Its primary function is to serve as the site of actual diffusion of $\text{O}_{2}$ and $\text{CO}_{2}$ between the blood and atmospheric air.

Answer: Alveoli and their ducts; site of actual diffusion of $\text{O}_{2}$ and $\text{CO}_{2}$ between blood and atmospheric air

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following types of joints is present between the carpal and metacarpal of the human thumb?
questions.solution:
The joint between the carpal and metacarpal of the human thumb is a saddle joint.

A pivot joint is present between the atlas and axis.

A gliding joint is present between the carpals.

A hinge joint is present in the knee and elbow.

Answer: Saddle joint

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Progestasert and LNG-20 are examples of which of the following types of contraceptive devices?
questions.solution:
Intrauterine Devices (IUDs) are classified into three main types:

Non-medicated IUDs: Examples include Lippes loop.

Copper releasing IUDs: Examples include CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375.

Hormone releasing IUDs: Examples include Progestasert and LNG-20. These devices release hormones that make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms.

Therefore, Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone releasing IUDs.

Answer: Hormone releasing IUDs

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
Which of the given features are characteristic of oogenesis but are absent in the process of spermatogenesis?

(a) No more gamete mother cells are formed and added after birth

(b) The meiotic division is temporarily arrested at the prophase-I stage

(c) A single primary gametocyte yields four functional haploid gametes

(d) The first meiotic division is unequal, producing a large haploid cell and a tiny polar body

(e) The process is regulated by the secretion of gonadotropins from the anterior pituitary

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement (a) is a characteristic of oogenesis because oogonia are formed only during embryonic development and no more are added after birth, whereas in spermatogenesis, spermatogonia continue to multiply after puberty.

Statement (b) is a characteristic of oogenesis because primary oocytes are arrested at the prophase-I stage of meiosis until puberty, whereas spermatogenesis is a continuous process without such arrest.

Statement (c) is incorrect for oogenesis because a single primary oocyte yields only one functional ovum and polar bodies, whereas a primary spermatocyte yields four functional spermatozoa.

Statement (d) is a characteristic of oogenesis because the first meiotic division is unequal, producing a large secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body, whereas in spermatogenesis, the division is equal.

Statement (e) is incorrect as a distinguishing feature because both oogenesis and spermatogenesis are regulated by gonadotropins (LH and FSH) secreted from the anterior pituitary.

Therefore, features (a), (b), and (d) are characteristic of oogenesis but absent in spermatogenesis.

Answer: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following events of oogenesis occurs specifically during the embryonic development stage in human females?
options: Completion of meiosis I to form a large secondary oocyte
Formation of a couple of million oogonia within each fetal ovary
Transition of primary follicles into mature Graafian follicles
Extrusion of the second polar body
questions.solution:
Oogenesis is initiated during the embryonic development stage when a couple of million gamete mother cells (oogonia) are formed within each fetal ovary. No more oogonia are formed and added after birth.

Completion of meiosis I occurs just prior to ovulation during the reproductive years.

Transition of primary follicles into mature Graafian follicles occurs during the menstrual cycle after puberty.

Extrusion of the second polar body occurs only after the entry of the sperm into the secondary oocyte (fertilization).

Answer: Formation of a couple of million oogonia within each fetal ovary

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the technique of DNA fingerprinting, the specific type of satellite DNA that shows a very high degree of polymorphism and was initially used as a probe by Alec Jeffreys is known as:
questions.solution:
Alec Jeffreys initially developed the technique of DNA fingerprinting. He used a specific type of satellite DNA as a probe that shows a very high degree of polymorphism. This satellite DNA is known as Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTRs).

Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) are used to identify all the genes that are expressed as RNA.

Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) refer to single base DNA differences.

Bacterial Artificial Chromosomes (BACs) are used as vectors for cloning large DNA fragments.

Answer: Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTRs)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In a particular strain of E. coli, a mutation occurs in the i gene such that the synthesized repressor protein completely loses its affinity for the operator region. Which of the following best describes the expression of the lac operon in this mutant strain?
options: Transcription of $z, y$ and $a$ genes will occur only when lactose is provided in the medium.
The operon will be transcribed continuously irrespective of the presence or absence of lactose.
The operon will remain permanently switched off even if the inducer is added.
Only the $z$ gene will be transcribed while $y$ and $a$ genes will remain repressed.
questions.solution:
The $i$ gene of the $lac$ operon codes for the repressor protein. Normally, this repressor binds to the operator region and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the structural genes ($z$, $y$, and $a$).

In the given mutant strain, the repressor protein loses its affinity for the operator region. As a result, it can no longer bind to the operator to block transcription.

Since the operator is never blocked by the repressor, RNA polymerase will continuously bind to the promoter and transcribe the structural genes. This results in the constitutive (continuous) expression of the $lac$ operon, regardless of whether the inducer (lactose) is present or absent in the medium.

Answer: The operon will be transcribed continuously irrespective of the presence or absence of lactose.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A researcher isolates a specific double-stranded DNA fragment that contains $2 \times 10^{5}$ base pairs. What will be the approximate physical length of this DNA fragment?
questions.solution:
The distance between two consecutive base pairs in a typical B-DNA double helix is $0.34 \text{ nm}$ or $0.34 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.

The total length of the DNA fragment is calculated by multiplying the total number of base pairs by the distance between two consecutive base pairs.

$\text{Length} = 2 \times 10^{5} \times 0.34 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$

$\text{Length} = 0.68 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$

Converting meters to micrometers ($\mu\text{m}$), where $1 \mu\text{m} = 10^{-6} \text{ m}$:

$\text{Length} = 68 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m} = 68 \mu\text{m}$

Answer: $68 \mu\text{m}$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: During the operation of natural selection, if the graphical representation of the trait distribution forms two distinct peaks, it indicates that:
options: more individuals acquire the mean character value.
more individuals acquire a specific character value other than the mean character value.
more individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve.
the population is maintaining Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium without any evolutionary change.
questions.solution:
Natural selection can lead to three main types of changes in the frequency distribution of traits: stabilizing, directional, and disruptive selection.

When the graphical representation of the trait distribution forms two distinct peaks, it indicates disruptive selection. In this type of selection, extreme phenotypes (peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve) are favored over intermediate phenotypes.

Option (A) represents stabilizing selection, where more individuals acquire the mean character value, leading to a narrower peak.

Option (B) represents directional selection, where more individuals acquire a specific character value other than the mean, shifting the peak in one direction.

Option (D) represents a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, where no natural selection or evolutionary change is occurring.

Answer: more individuals acquire peripheral character values at both ends of the distribution curve.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following microbes is used for the commercial production of blood-cholesterol lowering agents?
questions.solution:
Statins are used as blood-cholesterol lowering agents.

They are produced commercially by the yeast Monascus purpureus.

Statins act by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of cholesterol.

Streptococcus produces streptokinase, which is used as a clot buster.

Acetobacter aceti is used for the production of acetic acid.

Aspergillus niger is used for the production of citric acid.

Answer: Monascus purpureus

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Which of the following statements cannot be attributed to the ecological interaction of Parasitism?
options: It often drives co-evolution, where the host evolves mechanisms to reject the parasite and the parasite evolves to counteract them.
It acts as nature's primary conduit for transferring energy fixed by autotrophs to higher trophic levels.
It may render the host more vulnerable to other ecological pressures, such as predation, by making it physically weak.
It generally reduces the survival, growth, and reproductive fitness of the host organism, thereby decreasing its population density.
questions.solution:
Predation acts as nature's primary conduit for transferring energy fixed by plants (autotrophs) to higher trophic levels, not parasitism.

Parasitism is an interaction where one organism (parasite) benefits at the expense of the other (host). It often drives co-evolution between the host and the parasite. Parasites typically reduce the survival, growth, and reproductive fitness of the host, thereby decreasing its population density. They can also make the host physically weak, rendering it more vulnerable to other ecological pressures such as predation.

Therefore, the statement regarding the primary conduit for energy transfer is attributed to predation, not parasitism.

Answer: It acts as nature's primary conduit for transferring energy fixed by autotrophs to higher trophic levels.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: If in a pond there were $50$ water lily plants last year and through reproduction $15$ new plants are added this year, the birth rate in the population is ____ offspring per water lily per year.
questions.solution:
Initial population of water lily plants, $N = 50$

Number of new plants added through reproduction, $\Delta N = 15$

Time period, $\Delta t = 1$ year

Birth rate is calculated as the number of new individuals produced per unit of the initial population per unit time.

Birth rate $= \dfrac{\Delta N}{N \times \Delta t}$

Birth rate $= \dfrac{15}{50 \times 1} = 0.3$ offspring per water lily per year.

Answer: $0.3$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A research team working on a genome project decides to focus their efforts exclusively on identifying all the genes that are transcribed into RNA, while ignoring the non-coding regions. According to the methodologies established during the Human Genome Project, this strategy is known as:
questions.solution:
The methodologies of the Human Genome Project involved two major approaches.

One approach focused on identifying all the genes that are expressed as RNA. This approach is referred to as Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs).

The other approach was a blind approach of simply sequencing the whole set of genome that contained all the coding and non-coding sequence, and later assigning different regions in the sequence with functions. This is referred to as Sequence Annotation.

Since the research team focuses exclusively on identifying genes transcribed into RNA, the strategy is known as Expressed Sequence Tags.

Answer: Expressed Sequence Tags

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A culture of E. coli bacteria, with its DNA completely labeled with the heavy isotope $^{15}\text{N}$, is transferred to a medium containing the normal isotope $^{14}\text{N}$. After 80 minutes of growth, the DNA is extracted and analyzed via CsCl density gradient centrifugation. What will be the ratio of light DNA to hybrid DNA molecules in the sample?
questions.solution:
The generation time of E. coli is 20 minutes.

Number of generations in 80 minutes = $\dfrac{80}{20} = 4$.

Total number of DNA molecules after 4 generations = $2^4 = 16$.

Initially, the DNA is completely heavy ($^{15}\text{N}-^{15}\text{N}$), containing 2 heavy strands.

During replication in a $^{14}\text{N}$ medium, these 2 heavy strands separate and act as templates, forming exactly 2 hybrid DNA molecules ($^{15}\text{N}-^{14}\text{N}$) in all subsequent generations.

The remaining DNA molecules will be completely light ($^{14}\text{N}-^{14}\text{N}$).

Number of light DNA molecules = $16 - 2 = 14$.

Ratio of light DNA to hybrid DNA = $14 : 2 = 7 : 1$.

Answer: $7 : 1$

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q:
In a genetic mapping experiment, the crossing over frequencies between four linked genes P, Q, R, and S were recorded as follows:
P and S = $35\%$
Q and R = $15\%$
P and R = $25\%$
Q and S = $25\%$
R and S = $10\%$
P and Q = $10\%$

Based on this data, identify the correct linear order of these genes on the chromosome.
questions.solution:
Crossing over frequencies are directly proportional to the distance between genes on a chromosome, where $1\%$ crossing over equals $1$ map unit.

The maximum recombination frequency is between P and S ($35\%$), which means P and S are located at the two extreme ends of the gene map.

The distance between P and R is $25\%$, and between R and S is $10\%$. Since $25 + 10 = 35$, R must be located between P and S.

The distance between P and Q is $10\%$, and between Q and R is $15\%$. Since $10 + 15 = 25$, Q must be located between P and R.

Checking the remaining distance, Q and S is $25\%$. From the map, the distance from Q to S is the sum of Q to R ($15\%$) and R to S ($10\%$), which equals $25\%$. This confirms the arrangement.

Thus, the correct linear order of the genes on the chromosome is P, Q, R, S.

Answer: P, Q, R, S

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A phenotypically normal woman, whose father suffered from haemophilia, marries a normal man. What percentage of their total progeny is expected to be affected by haemophilia?
questions.solution:
Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder. Let the normal allele be $X^{H}$ and the haemophilia allele be $X^{h}$.

The genotype of the woman's father is $X^{h}Y$.

Since the woman is phenotypically normal but her father was haemophilic, she must have inherited the $X^{h}$ chromosome from him. Thus, she is a carrier and her genotype is $X^{H}X^{h}$.

The woman marries a normal man, whose genotype is $X^{H}Y$.

The cross is $X^{H}X^{h} \times X^{H}Y$.

The possible genotypes of the progeny are:
$X^{H}X^{H}$ (Normal female) - $25\%$
$X^{H}X^{h}$ (Carrier female, phenotypically normal) - $25\%$
$X^{H}Y$ (Normal male) - $25\%$
$X^{h}Y$ (Haemophilic male) - $25\%$

The only affected progeny is the haemophilic male ($X^{h}Y$).

Therefore, the percentage of the total progeny expected to be affected by haemophilia is $25\%$.

Answer: $25\%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere and a thin hollow spherical shell have the same mass and the same radius. The ratio of the radius of gyration of the solid sphere to that of the hollow spherical shell, about their respective diametric axes, is:
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its diametric axis is $I_1 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$

Radius of gyration of the solid sphere is $K_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_1}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R$

Moment of inertia of a thin hollow spherical shell about its diametric axis is $I_2 = \dfrac{2}{3}MR^2$

Radius of gyration of the hollow spherical shell is $K_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_2}{M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}R$

The ratio of their radii of gyration is $\dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R}{\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}R} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{5}}$

The ratio is $\sqrt{3} : \sqrt{5}$

Answer: $\sqrt{3} : \sqrt{5}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two cylindrical wires, A and B, are made of the same material and have identical lengths. The radius of wire A is twice the radius of wire B. If these two wires are connected in series across a constant voltage source, what will be the ratio of the heat dissipated in wire A to that in wire B during the same time interval?
questions.solution:
Resistance of a cylindrical wire is given by $R = \rho \dfrac{L}{\pi r^2}$.

Since both wires have the same material ($\rho$) and length ($L$), the resistance is inversely proportional to the square of the radius: $R \propto \dfrac{1}{r^2}$.

Given $r_A = 2r_B$, the ratio of their resistances is:

$\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \left(\dfrac{r_B}{r_A}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{r_B}{2r_B}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

When connected in series, the same current $I$ flows through both wires. The heat dissipated in time $t$ is $H = I^2 R t$.

Since $I$ and $t$ are constant, $H \propto R$.

Therefore, the ratio of heat dissipated is:

$\dfrac{H_A}{H_B} = \dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Answer: $1:4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : According to Biot-Savart's law, the magnitude of the magnetic field produced by a current element is inversely proportional to the cube of the distance between the element and the observation point.

Statement II : The direction of the magnetic field $d\vec{B}$ produced by a current element $I d\vec{l}$ is always perpendicular to the plane containing the current element and the position vector $\vec{r}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
According to Biot-Savart's law, the magnetic field due to a current element is given by $d\vec{B} = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{I d\vec{l} \times \vec{r}}{r^3}$.

The magnitude of the magnetic field is $dB = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{I dl \sin\theta}{r^2}$. This shows that the magnitude of the magnetic field is inversely proportional to the square of the distance $r$, not the cube. Hence, Statement I is incorrect.

The direction of $d\vec{B}$ is determined by the cross product $d\vec{l} \times \vec{r}$. By the properties of the cross product, $d\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to both $d\vec{l}$ and $\vec{r}$, which means it is perpendicular to the plane containing the current element and the position vector. Hence, Statement II is correct.

Answer: Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plano-convex lens made of a material with a refractive index of $1.6$ has a power of $+4.0\text{ D}$. What is the radius of curvature of its curved surface?
questions.solution:
Using the lens maker's formula:

$P = (\mu - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$

For a plano-convex lens, the radius of curvature of the plane surface is infinity. Let $R_1 = R$ and $R_2 = \infty$.

$P = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{R}$

Given $P = +4.0\text{ D}$ and $\mu = 1.6$:

$4.0 = \dfrac{1.6 - 1}{R}$

$4.0 = \dfrac{0.6}{R}$

$R = \dfrac{0.6}{4.0} = 0.15\text{ m}$

$R = 15\text{ cm}$

Answer: $15\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The given graph shows the variation of de Broglie wavelength ($\lambda$) with the inverse of velocity ($1/v$) for two different particles A and B. If $m_A$ and $m_B$ are the respective masses of particles A and B, which of the following relations is correct?
options: The relationship depends on the charges of the particles
questions.solution:
The de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ of a particle is given by the relation:

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

This can be rewritten as:

$\lambda = \left(\dfrac{h}{m}\right) \left(\dfrac{1}{v}\right)$

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line $y = mx$, the graph of $\lambda$ versus $1/v$ is a straight line passing through the origin with a slope equal to $\dfrac{h}{m}$.

From the given graph, the slope of line A is greater than the slope of line B.

$\text{Slope}_A \gt \text{Slope}_B$

$\dfrac{h}{m_A} \gt \dfrac{h}{m_B}$

Since $h$ is a positive constant, this implies:

$m_A \lt m_B$

Answer: $m_A \lt m_B$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
(a)Coefficient of viscosity(i)$[M L^{2} T^{-2}]$
(b)Surface tension(ii)$[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$
(c)Modulus of elasticity(iii)$[M L^{-1} T^{-1}]$
(d)Torque(iv)$[M L^{0} T^{-2}]$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Coefficient of viscosity, $\eta = \dfrac{F}{A \left(\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right)}$

$[\eta] = \dfrac{[M L T^{-2}]}{[L^{2}] [T^{-1}]} = [M L^{-1} T^{-1}]$

Surface tension, $S = \dfrac{F}{l}$

$[S] = \dfrac{[M L T^{-2}]}{[L]} = [M L^{0} T^{-2}]$

Modulus of elasticity, $E = \dfrac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}}$

$[E] = \dfrac{[M L T^{-2}] / [L^{2}]}{[M^{0} L^{0} T^{0}]} = [M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$

Torque, $\tau = r \times F$

$[\tau] = [L] [M L T^{-2}] = [M L^{2} T^{-2}]$

Thus, the correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i).

Answer: (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a load is suspended from a vertical helical spring, the volume of the wire used to make the spring remains practically constant.

Reason (R): The extension of a helical spring is determined by the shear modulus of its material, and shearing strain does not produce any change in volume.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
When a load is suspended from a vertical helical spring, the wire of the spring is subjected to torsional shear stress. The elongation of the spring is primarily due to the twisting of the wire.

The spring constant is given by $k = \dfrac{G r^4}{4 R^3 N}$, where $G$ is the shear modulus of the material. This shows that the extension of the spring is determined by the shear modulus.

Since the deformation is purely due to shear strain, and shear strain involves only a change in shape without any change in volume, the volume of the wire remains practically constant.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long straight solid cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ carries a steady current uniformly distributed over its cross-section. The magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance $r = \dfrac{R}{4}$ from the axis of the conductor is $B$. At what distance from the axis, outside the conductor, will the magnitude of the magnetic field again be equal to $B$?
questions.solution:
For a long straight solid cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ carrying a steady current $I$ uniformly distributed over its cross-section, the magnetic field at a distance $r$ from the axis is given by Ampere's law.

Inside the conductor ($r \lt R$):
$B_{in} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2 \pi R^2}$

Outside the conductor ($r \gt R$):
$B_{out} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r}$

At a distance $r = \dfrac{R}{4}$ inside the conductor, the magnetic field is:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi R^2} \left( \dfrac{R}{4} \right) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{8 \pi R}$

Let the distance outside the conductor where the magnetic field is again $B$ be $r'$. Then:
$B_{out} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r'} = B$

Substituting the value of $B$:
$\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2 \pi r'} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{8 \pi R}$

Solving for $r'$:
$2 \pi r' = 8 \pi R$

$r' = 4R$

Answer: $4R$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the shape and size of atomic orbitals is correct?
options: All five $3d$ orbitals possess identical shapes and differ only in their spatial orientation.
The $4d_{xy}$ orbital is larger in size than the $3d_{xy}$ orbital, but both possess the same number of angular nodes.
The electron probability density for the $3d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital is zero along the x and y axes.
The $2s$ and $3s$ orbitals are spherically symmetric and have an equal number of radial nodes.
questions.solution:
For option (A), four of the $3d$ orbitals ($d_{xy}$, $d_{yz}$, $d_{zx}$, $d_{x^2-y^2}$) have a double-dumbbell shape, while the fifth ($d_{z^2}$) has a dumbbell shape with a doughnut-shaped electron cloud around its center. Thus, they do not all possess identical shapes.

For option (B), as the principal quantum number $n$ increases, the size of the orbital increases. Therefore, the $4d_{xy}$ orbital is larger than the $3d_{xy}$ orbital. The number of angular nodes is given by the azimuthal quantum number $l$. For any $d$ orbital, $l = 2$, so both $4d_{xy}$ and $3d_{xy}$ possess $2$ angular nodes. This statement is correct.

For option (C), the lobes of the $3d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital are directed along the x and y axes. Hence, the electron probability density is maximum along these axes, not zero.

For option (D), the number of radial nodes is given by $n - l - 1$. For the $2s$ orbital, the number of radial nodes is $2 - 0 - 1 = 1$. For the $3s$ orbital, it is $3 - 0 - 1 = 2$. They do not have an equal number of radial nodes.

Answer: The $4d_{xy}$ orbital is larger in size than the $3d_{xy}$ orbital, but both possess the same number of angular nodes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling point of $NH_3$ is the highest among all the hydrides of Group 15 elements.
Statement II: The higher boiling point of $NH_3$ compared to $PH_3$ is due to the presence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect because the boiling point of $NH_3$ is not the highest among Group 15 hydrides. The boiling point order is $PH_3 \lt AsH_3 \lt NH_3 \lt SbH_3 \lt BiH_3$. The boiling points of $SbH_3$ and $BiH_3$ are higher than that of $NH_3$ due to stronger van der Waals forces resulting from their larger size and higher molecular mass.

Statement II is correct because $NH_3$ exhibits intermolecular hydrogen bonding due to the high electronegativity and small size of nitrogen, which is absent in $PH_3$. This leads to a higher boiling point for $NH_3$ compared to $PH_3$.

Therefore, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
options: The $B_2$ molecule is diamagnetic in nature because it contains an even number of electrons.
The species $N_2^+$ and $N_2^-$ have identical bond orders, but $N_2^+$ is more stable than $N_2^-$.
In the $O_2$ molecule, the energy of the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ molecular orbital is higher than that of the degenerate $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals.
The $He_2^+$ ion has a calculated bond order of $1.0$.
questions.solution:
For the $B_2$ molecule, the total number of electrons is $10$. The molecular orbital electronic configuration is $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^{1} = \pi_{2p_y}^{1}$. Due to the presence of two unpaired electrons, $B_2$ is paramagnetic. Thus, statement (A) is incorrect.

For $N_2^{+}$, the total number of electrons is $13$. The bond order is $\dfrac{1}{2}(9 - 4) = 2.5$.
For $N_2^{-}$, the total number of electrons is $15$. The bond order is $\dfrac{1}{2}(10 - 5) = 2.5$.
Both species have the same bond order, but $N_2^{-}$ has more electrons in antibonding molecular orbitals ($5$) compared to $N_2^{+}$ ($4$). Therefore, $N_2^{+}$ is more stable than $N_2^{-}$. Thus, statement (B) is correct.

In the $O_2$ molecule, the order of energy of molecular orbitals is $\sigma_{2p_z} \lt  \pi_{2p_x} = \pi_{2p_y} \lt  \pi_{2p_x}^{*} = \pi_{2p_y}^{*} \lt  \sigma_{2p_z}^{*}$. The energy of the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital is lower than that of the degenerate $\pi_{2p_x}$ and $\pi_{2p_y}$ orbitals. Thus, statement (C) is incorrect.

For the $He_2^{+}$ ion, the total number of electrons is $3$. The configuration is $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*1}$. The bond order is $\dfrac{1}{2}(2 - 1) = 0.5$. Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

Answer: The species $N_2^+$ and $N_2^-$ have identical bond orders, but $N_2^+$ is more stable than $N_2^-$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling point of hydrogen fluoride ($HF$) is significantly higher than that of hydrogen chloride ($HCl$).
Statement II: $HF$ molecules are associated in the liquid state due to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas $HCl$ molecules interact primarily through weaker dipole-dipole forces.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct because the boiling point of $HF$ is much higher than that of $HCl$.

Statement II is correct because fluorine is highly electronegative and small in size, leading to strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding in $HF$. In contrast, chlorine is larger and less electronegative, so $HCl$ molecules interact mainly through weaker dipole-dipole interactions.

Therefore, both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding stereoisomerism?
options: Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other.
Meso compounds are optically active because they possess chiral carbon atoms.
A racemic mixture is optically inactive due to internal compensation.
Enantiomers possess identical physical properties such as melting point, boiling point, and refractive index.
questions.solution:
Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other.

Meso compounds contain chiral centers but are optically inactive due to the presence of a plane or center of symmetry, which leads to internal compensation.

A racemic mixture is an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers and is optically inactive due to external compensation.

Enantiomers have identical physical properties such as melting point, boiling point, density, and refractive index. They only differ in their interaction with plane-polarized light and chiral reagents.

Answer: Enantiomers possess identical physical properties such as melting point, boiling point, and refractive index.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are half cell reactions :

$Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O$,
$E^\circ_{Cr^{3+}/Cr_2O_7^{2-}} = -1.33\text{ V}$

$Cl_2 + 2e^- \rightarrow 2Cl^-$,
$E^\circ_{Cl_2/Cl^-} = +1.36\text{ V}$

Will the dichromate ion, $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$, oxidize $Cl^-$ to $Cl_2$ gas in an acidic medium under standard conditions?
questions.solution:
The given standard oxidation potential of $Cr^{3+}$ to $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is $E^\circ_{Cr^{3+}/Cr_2O_7^{2-}} = -1.33\text{ V}$.

The standard reduction potential of $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ is $E^\circ_{Cr_2O_7^{2-}/Cr^{3+}} = +1.33\text{ V}$.

The standard reduction potential of $Cl_2$ is $E^\circ_{Cl_2/Cl^-} = +1.36\text{ V}$.

For the oxidation of $Cl^-$ by $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$, the dichromate ion undergoes reduction (cathode) and the chloride ion undergoes oxidation (anode).

The standard cell potential is calculated as:

$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}}$

$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{Cr_2O_7^{2-}/Cr^{3+}} - E^\circ_{Cl_2/Cl^-}$

$E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.33\text{ V} - 1.36\text{ V} = -0.03\text{ V}$

Since $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ is negative, the reaction is non-spontaneous. Therefore, $Cr_2O_7^{2-}$ will not oxidize $Cl^-$ to $Cl_2$ gas.

Answer: No, because $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -0.03\text{ V}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The standard reduction potentials of $Cr^{3+}/Cr$, $Cd^{2+}/Cd$, $Co^{2+}/Co$, and $Sn^{2+}/Sn$ are $-0.74\text{ V}$, $-0.40\text{ V}$, $-0.28\text{ V}$, and $-0.14\text{ V}$ respectively.

Based on these values, which of the following reactions is spontaneous under standard conditions?
questions.solution:
For a reaction to be spontaneous under standard conditions, the standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{cell}$ must be positive.

$E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cathode} - E^{\circ}_{anode}$

A metal with a more negative standard reduction potential acts as the anode (undergoes oxidation) and can reduce the ion of a metal with a less negative standard reduction potential.

The given standard reduction potentials are:
$E^{\circ}(Cr^{3+}/Cr) = -0.74\text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}(Cd^{2+}/Cd) = -0.40\text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}(Co^{2+}/Co) = -0.28\text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}(Sn^{2+}/Sn) = -0.14\text{ V}$

The reducing power of the metals follows the order: $Cr \gt Cd \gt Co \gt Sn$.

Evaluating the given options:

For $Sn(s) + CoCl_2(aq) \rightarrow SnCl_2(aq) + Co(s)$:
$E^{\circ}_{cell} = -0.28 - (-0.14) = -0.14\text{ V} \lt 0$ (Non-spontaneous)

For $Co(s) + CdCl_2(aq) \rightarrow CoCl_2(aq) + Cd(s)$:
$E^{\circ}_{cell} = -0.40 - (-0.28) = -0.12\text{ V} \lt 0$ (Non-spontaneous)

For $3Cd(s) + 2CrCl_3(aq) \rightarrow 3CdCl_2(aq) + 2Cr(s)$:
$E^{\circ}_{cell} = -0.74 - (-0.40) = -0.34\text{ V} \lt 0$ (Non-spontaneous)

For $2Cr(s) + 3SnCl_2(aq) \rightarrow 2CrCl_3(aq) + 3Sn(s)$:
$E^{\circ}_{cell} = -0.14 - (-0.74) = +0.60\text{ V} \gt 0$ (Spontaneous)

Thus, the reaction between $Cr(s)$ and $SnCl_2(aq)$ is spontaneous.

Answer: $2Cr(s) + 3SnCl_2(aq) \rightarrow 2CrCl_3(aq) + 3Sn(s)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct IUPAC name for the coordination compound $[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]$?
questions.solution:
The given coordination compound is $[Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]$.

The complex consists of a cationic part $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{x+}$ and an anionic part $[Cr(CN)_6]^{y-}$.

Let the oxidation states of Co and Cr be $+3$ each, which are their most stable and common oxidation states in such coordination spheres. This gives the cation as $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$ and the anion as $[Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}$, balancing the charges.

According to IUPAC nomenclature rules, the cation is named first followed by the anion.

For the complex cation $[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}$, the ligand is ammine. There are six ammine ligands, so it is hexaammine. The central metal is cobalt in the $+3$ oxidation state. Thus, the name of the cation is hexaamminecobalt(III).

For the complex anion $[Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}$, the ligand is cyanido. There are six cyanido ligands, so it is hexacyanido. Since the complex is an anion, the suffix '-ate' is added to the metal name, making it chromate. The central metal is chromium in the $+3$ oxidation state. Thus, the name of the anion is hexacyanidochromate(III).

Combining both parts, the complete IUPAC name is hexaamminecobalt(III) hexacyanidochromate(III).

Answer: hexaamminecobalt(III) hexacyanidochromate(III)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: $p$-Methoxyphenol is a weaker acid than phenol because the $-OCH_{3}$ group destabilizes the phenoxide ion through its $+R$ effect.

Statement II: $m$-Methoxyphenol is also a weaker acid than phenol because the $+R$ effect of the $-OCH_{3}$ group operates at the meta position as well.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.solution:
The acidity of phenols depends on the stability of the phenoxide ion formed after the loss of a proton.

In $p$-methoxyphenol, the $-OCH_{3}$ group is at the para position. It exerts both a $-I$ (inductive) effect and a $+R$ (resonance) effect. At the para position, the $+R$ effect dominates over the $-I$ effect. The electron-donating $+R$ effect increases the electron density on the phenoxide oxygen, destabilizing the phenoxide ion. Thus, $p$-methoxyphenol is a weaker acid than phenol. Statement I is correct.

In $m$-methoxyphenol, the $-OCH_{3}$ group is at the meta position. The resonance effect ($+R$) does not operate at the meta position. Only the electron-withdrawing inductive effect ($-I$) operates, which stabilizes the phenoxide ion. Therefore, $m$-methoxyphenol is a stronger acid than phenol. Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

questions.solution:
Semicarbazone is formed when a carbonyl compound reacts with semicarbazide ($NH_2NHCONH_2$). Thus, A matches with 4.

Hydrazone is formed when a carbonyl compound reacts with hydrazine ($NH_2NH_2$). Thus, B matches with 1.
